i: 1 pound russet potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/2 inch thick
½ teaspoon table salt, plus salt for cooking potatoes
4 ounces (113 grams) sharp cheddar cheese, shredded (1 cup)
2 ½ cups (13¾ ounces/390 grams) bread flour
½ teaspoon table salt, plus salt for cooking pierogi
d:
FOR THE FILLING: Combine potatoes and 1 tablespoon salt in large saucepan and cover with water by 1 inch. Bring to boil over medium-high heat; reduce heat to medium and cook at vigorous simmer until potatoes are very tender, about 15 minutes.

Drain potatoes in colander. While still hot, combine potatoes, cheddar, butter, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper in bowl of stand mixer. Fit mixer with paddle and mix on medium speed until potatoes are smooth and all ingredients are fully combined, about 1 minute. Transfer filling to 8-inch square baking dish and refrigerate until fully chilled, about 30 minutes, or cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 24 hours.

FOR THE DOUGH: Whisk flour, baking powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt together in clean bowl of stand mixer. Add sour cream and egg and yolk. Fit mixer with dough hook and knead on medium-high speed for 8 minutes (dough will be smooth and elastic). Transfer dough to floured bowl, cover with plastic, and refrigerate until ready to assemble.

Line rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and dust with flour. Roll dough on lightly floured counter into 18-inch circle, about 1/8 inch thick. Using 3-inch biscuit cutter, cut 20 to 24 circles from dough. Place 1 tablespoon chilled filling in center of each dough round. Fold dough over filling to create half-moon shape and pinch edges firmly to seal. Transfer to prepared sheet.

Gather dough scraps and reroll to 1/8-inch thickness. Cut 6 to 10 more circles from dough and repeat with remaining filling. (It may be necessary to reroll dough once more to yield 30 pierogi.) Cover pierogi with plastic and refrigerate until ready to cook, up to 3 hours.

FOR THE TOPPING: Melt butter in 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat. Add onion and salt and cook until onion is caramelized, 15 to 20 minutes. Remove skillet from heat and set aside.

Bring 4 quarts water to boil in Dutch oven. Add 1 tablespoon salt and half of pierogi to boiling water and cook until tender, about 5 minutes. Using spider or slotted spoon, remove pierogi from water and transfer to skillet with caramelized onion. Return water to boil, cook remaining pierogi, and transfer to skillet with first batch.

Add 2 tablespoons cooking water to pierogi in skillet. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring gently, until onion mixture is warmed through and adhered to pierogi. Transfer to platter and serve.

TO MAKE AHEAD: Uncooked pierogi can be frozen for several weeks. After sealing pierogi in step 4, freeze them on baking sheet, about 3 hours. Transfer frozen pierogi to zipper-lock freezer bag. When ready to cook, extend boiling time in step 7 to about 7 minutes.

i: One 5-pound pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch cubes

d:
Heat an electric pressure cooker on the saute mode. When hot, add half of the olive oil. Add half of the pork along with half of the salt, chili powder, black pepper, garlic powder and onion powder. Saute until the meat is very crisp and brown, about 10 minutes. Set the meat aside on a plate. Add the remaining olive oil, meat, salt, chili powder, black pepper, garlic powder and onion powder and cook until the meat is crisp and brown, another 10 minutes.

Add the first half of the meat back to the pressure cooker. Add the garlic and onions and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes. Pour in the chicken stock. Follow the manufacturer's guide for locking the lid and preparing to cook. Set to pressure cook on manual for 40 minutes.

After the pressure-cook cycle is complete, follow the manufacturer's guide for natural release. After 15 minutes, release the rest of the steam using quick release.

Remove the lid from the pressure cooker. Remove the pork and onions to a baking sheet. Shred the pork with 2 forks, pour over the barbecue sauce and toss to coat. Serve with the buns and Pickled Jalapenos and Onions.

If not serving right away, transfer to a 9-by-13-inch disposable aluminum pan, cover with foil and keep warm in the oven at 300 degrees F until ready to serve.

Pickled Jalapenos and Onions:

Put the jalapenos and red onions in a 16-ounce wide-mouth mason jar.

In a small saucepan, combine the vinegar, sugar, salt and 1 cup water. Bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar and salt are dissolved.

Pour the hot liquid over the veggies in the jar, screw on the lid and set aside. When it has cooled to room temperature, transfer the jar to the fridge to chill for a minimum of an hour, which will allow the vegetables to pickle. The pickles will last in the fridge for 3 days. Serve them on pulled pork sandwiches.

no:
Chicken: I recommend grilling apple cider vinegar chicken or making my air fryer chicken breast.

Spinach: If you’re not a spinach fan, feel free to use your favorite leafy green instead. spring mix or arugula would be my next choice of greens for this salad.

Dressing: I love the citrus poppyseed dressing paired with this salad but any dressing would work if you’re in a pinch. Some options: balsamic dressing, white balsamic vinaigrette or lemon vinaigrette.

Mix-ins: Feel free to switch up your mix-ins for this salad… I often do! Sometimes I change up the veggies based on what I have on hand. Feel free to get creative and make this salad your own.

Grains: I love adding grains to my salad for some extra volume and nutrients. Toss in cooked quinoa, rice or farro to make this a heartier salad.

d:
1. Char the Corn First

* Oil the flat top lightly
* Cook corn until blistered and lightly charred
* Pull off and let cool slightly

2. Build the Street Corn Mix

In a large bowl:

* Corn + mayo + sour cream
* Cotija + garlic + lime juice
* Red onion + cilantro + chili powder

Mix well.

Taste and adjust:

* Needs pop? → more lime
* Too rich? → pinch of salt + more lime
* Too sharp? → small spoon of mayo

You want it bright, creamy, and just slightly salty

3. Prep the Chicken

* Mix chicken with all seasoning until evenly combined
* Divide into ~2.5 oz balls (golf ball size)

* Light oil on flat top
* Place chicken ball down
* Immediately place tortilla on top
* Smash firmly (pressing chicken into tortilla)

Cook 3–4 minutes until:

* Chicken gets crispy edges
* Tortilla starts to firm up

Flip and cook another 2–3 minutes until tortilla is golden and slightly crisp.

Don’t rush this. The crispy layer = the payoff.

5. Build Each Taco

* Spoon on street corn mix
* Drizzle chipotle crema (optional)
* Squeeze fresh lime
* Finish with Maldon salt

Cook the noodles. Brown the beef with the onion and mushrooms.

Add the garlic and flour, then the broth and Worcestershire. Simmer 5 minutes until thick.

Off the heat, stir in the sour cream. Serve over the noodles.

i: 3/4 cup small-torn pieces of gluten free white bread (no crusts)
2 mozzarella cheese sticks, cut in half
1 jar gluten free marinara or spaghetti sauce
d:
Preheat oven to 425 degrees then line a half or quarter sheet pan with foil and spray with nonstick spray. Set aside.

Add torn bread plus grated onion and juices into a large bowl then stir to combine and let sit for a minute. Add parmesan cheese, egg, garlic, parsley, and lots of salt and pepper then stir to combine. Crumble ground beef on top then use your hands to combine ingredients. Divide mixture into four equal portions then form each portion into an oval. n: Summer Bowtie Pasta and Chicken Sausage Skillet Bake
i: 2 medium zucchini (about 1 lb.), sliced into 1/4"-thick rounds
1 medium red bell pepper, seeded, chopped
1/2 cup fresh basil leaves, torn, plus more for serving
d:
Preheat oven to 375º. In a large pot of boiling salted water, cook pasta, stirring occasionally, until very al dente, 2 to 3 minutes less than package instructions. Drain pasta and return to pot. Toss with marinara and set aside.

In a large, high-sided, ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat, heat 1 tablespoon oil. Add sausage and cook, tossing occasionally, until golden on both sides, about 3 minutes. Transfer sausage to pot with pasta.

In same skillet over medium-high heat, heat remaining 2 tablespoons oil. Cook zucchini, bell pepper, black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and vegetables are crisp-tender, about 3 minutes.

Add garlic to skillet, and cook, stirring, until fragrant and golden, about 1 minute. Add spinach and cook, tossing, until wilted, about 2 minutes more. Scrape vegetable mixture into pot with pasta, add basil, and toss to combine; reserve skillet.

Spoon half of pasta mixture into reserved skillet. Top with 1 1/2 cups mozzarella. Scrape remaining pasta mixture over and top with remaining 1 1/2 cups mozzarella.

Bake until cheese is melted and top is golden brown, 14 to 16 minutes. Let cool 5 minutes. Top with more basil before serving.

Top with basil leaves and zest from 1 lemon. Cut zested lemon into wedges and serve alongside. Let sit 5 minutes before serving.

Make Pancake Batter: Blend the eggs and milk until doubled in size, about 30 seconds. Add flour, melted butter, sugar, and salt; blend for another 15-20 seconds until combined.

Pour and Pan Tilt: Preheat a nonstick or well seasoned cast iron pan over medium heat. Pour about 1/4 cup of pancake batter into the pan with one hand, and immediately tilt the pan with the other hand to spread the batter even wider. This will give you a signature thin lacy edge on your pancake.

Cook: Let it sit for about 1 minute or until the pancake is golden brown; use a spatula to pull the edges up and flip the pancake. Cook for another 15-30 seconds on the back side. You can cook to your desired level of doneness; I prefer golden brown on the front side and pale on the back side.

1/2 cup low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth

Cut in half on the diagonal.

i: 6–7 lb chuck roast (two smaller roasts if needed)
3 large carrots, cut into big chunks
Zest of 1 orange (no juice — keeps things savory)
1–2 tbsp apple cider vinegar (added after cooking for brightness)
d:
INSTRUCTIONS

1. Season and sear

Pat roasts dry.
Season all sides with the 4 tsp salt + 2 tsp pepper.

Set Instant Pot to Sauté – High.
Add oil and sear each roast 3–4 minutes per side.
Remove and set aside.

2. Build the base

Add onions, carrots, and celery to the pot.
Sauté 3–4 minutes until lightly softened.
Add garlic and cook 30 seconds.

Stir in:
 • Soy sauce
 • Worcestershire
 • Dijon mustard

Scrape up browned bits.

3. Add liquids and aromatics

Pour in:
 • Beef broth
 • Apple cider

Add:
 • Fresh cranberries
 • Orange zest
 • Rosemary
 • Thyme
 • Bay leaves

Stir well.

Fresh cranberries dissolve during pressure cooking and only leave background acidity, not “cranberry flavor.”

4. Pressure cook

Place roasts back into the pot.
Seal lid.

Set to Pressure Cook – High – 70 minutes.
Allow 15 minutes natural release, then quick release.

5. Shred and reduce

Transfer roasts to a large sheet pan or bowl.

Set Instant Pot to Sauté – High and reduce the cooking liquid 10–12 minutes until slightly thickened.

Whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter for smoothness.

Taste.
Add 1–2 tbsp apple cider vinegar to bring the sauce to life.

Season to taste with kosher salt.

6. Serve

Shred the beef into large rustic pieces.
Place on a platter and pour the jus over the top or serve sauce on the side.
Finish with a light sprinkle of Maldon salt just before serving.

i: 4 pounds potatoes russet or Yukon gold
d:
Peel and quarter potatoes, place in a pot of cold salted water.

Add cloves of garlic (if using) & bring to a boil, cook uncovered 15 minutes or until fork-tender. Drain well.

Heat milk on the stove top (or in the microwave) until warm.

Add butter to the potatoes and begin mashing. Pour in heated milk a little at a time while using a potato masher to reach desired consistency.

Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot.
no:
Drain Well: I usually let them sit about 5 minutes or so to completely drain, or even drain well and put them back in the warm pot for a few minutes to make sure all liquid is evaporated.

Mash by Hand: Use a hand masher or a potato ricer for the creamiest potatoes. A hand mixer, stand mixer or food processor can work, but it can also break down the starches in the potatoes and cause a gummy texture.

Add BUTTER! There are places you can skimp on the butter and this is not one of them. I like to use salted butter and lots of it (but you can use unsalted and season potatoes to taste). Butter adds a creamy and... well, buttery texture.

Heat the Cream: Heat your milk/cream before adding. This keeps the potatoes hot and it absorbs better. Add cream/milk a little a time to get the right consistency.

i: 2 large boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 8 ounces each)

d:
Set a wire rack inside a rimmed baking sheet. Line another rimmed baking sheet with foil. Cut two 12-inch sheets of plastic wrap.

Cut the chicken breasts in half lengthwise, making 4 roughly equal pieces; they should look like large chicken tenders. Place one sheet of plastic on a clean cutting board. Put one chicken piece in the center of the plastic and top with the other sheet of plastic. Pound the chicken with the flat side of a meat mallet, starting in the center and working your way to the edges, until the chicken is 1/4-inch thick. Transfer to the wire rack. Repeat with the remaining chicken, one piece at a time. Liberally sprinkle with salt and pepper.

Put the flour in a pie plate and dredge the chicken 1 piece at a time, turning to coat and packing the flour into the crevices. Shake to remove any excess and return to the rack. Repeat with the remaining chicken.

Whisk the breadcrumbs, 1/4 cup of the Parmesan, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a medium bowl until combined. Whisk the milk and egg in a medium bowl until combined. Dip the dredged chicken into the milk mixture, allowing any excess to drip off. Then pack the seasoned breadcrumbs firmly onto the chicken. Very gently

shake off any excess and return to the rack. Refrigerate uncovered at least 30 minutes and up to 12 hours.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Heat 1/3 cup of the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the garlic, oregano and red pepper flakes and cook until very fragrant but not brown, about 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, basil and 1 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil and then reduce to a simmer and cook, uncovered, until the tomatoes are very tender and the liquid has reduced by half, about 30 minutes. Smash the tomatoes with a potato masher until almost smooth; it's ok if it's a little chunky. Season with salt.

Heat the remaining 1/2 cup oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 cutlets and cook until the coating is golden brown, about 1 minute per side; the chicken will not be cooked through. Transfer to the foil-lined baking sheet in a single layer 3 inches apart. Repeat with the remaining cutlets.

Arrange an oven rack directly under the broiler and preheat to high. Arrange the chicken in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, spaced 3 inches apart. Top each cutlet with 2/3 cup of the sauce and spread evenly to coat. Sprinkle each cutlet with 1 tablespoon of the Parmesan and 1/2 cup mozzarella. Broil until the cheese melts and starts to brown in spots, 2 to 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Cook the spaghetti, stirring occasionally, until al dente. Drain and transfer to the remaining sauce. Gently stir until the sauce coats the pasta. Transfer the spaghetti to a serving dish and top with the chicken. Sprinkle with more Parmesan and serve with torn basil.

i: 1 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting (see Cook's Note)

8 ounces slab bacon, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
d:
For the pastry crust: Pulse the flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a food processor until combined. Add the butter and pulse until the flour looks like cornmeal. Sprinkle in 3 tablespoons ice water and pulse until the dough begins to come together. Pinch the dough with your fingers; if it doesn't hold together, add up to 2 more tablespoons ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, and pulse again.

Transfer the dough to a sheet of plastic wrap and pat into a disc. Wrap tightly and refrigerate until firm, at least 1 hour and preferably overnight.

Lightly flour a work surface, then roll the dough into an 11-inch round, about 1/8 inch thick. Center the dough in a 9-inch fluted tart pan with removable bottom, with an even overhang of dough all around. Press the dough into the edges of the pan and the fluted sides. Roll the rolling pin over the top to cut off the extra dough (discard the extra). Poke the bottom and sides all over with a fork. Chill until completely cold, about 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, position an oven rack in the lower third of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees F.

Press a piece of parchment over the chilled crust, then fill with pie weights, raw beans or rice. Put the pan on a baking sheet. Bake until the crust is set and golden around the edges, about 40 minutes. Carefully remove the parchment and weights. Return to the oven and bake until the crust is dry and slightly golden, about 15 minutes more. Let cool completely, about 30 minutes.

For the filling: Combine the butter, onion, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/2 cup water in a medium skillet over medium-low heat. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions are completely softened and all the water has evaporated, about 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a separate medium skillet over medium-low heat, stirring, until the fat has rendered and the bacon is crisp, 10 to 15 minutes.

When the onions have cooked for 30 minutes, add the bacon using a slotted spoon, then stir in 1 teaspoon of the thyme and 1/2 teaspoon pepper. Spread the onion mixture in the bottom of the crust and sprinkle with the Gruyere. Whisk together the cream, eggs and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a medium bowl until combined. Pour the cream mixture over the filling in the crust and top with the remaining 1 teaspoon thyme.

Bake the quiche on the baking sheet until set and golden, about 30 minutes. Let cool at least 30 minutes before serving.

Mix together those ingredients, cover and keep at 78 degrees Fahrenheit. The levain should be ready in about 12 hours.

If you want to make a levain for the same day, mix together 70 grams ripe sourdough starter, 70 grams flour and 70 grams water. Leave it at 78 degrees F for about 3-4 hours until bubbly and ripe.

Mixing Sourdough Monkey Bread Dough

Set the bowl of a stand mixer on a kitchen scale and add the ingredients to the bowl. Mix together for about 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, pulls away from the sides of the bowl and can pass the windowpane test. The dough should be tacky, but not overly sticky. If it feels too sticky, add a little more flour just 10 grams at a time.

Bulk Fermentation

Remove the dough from the mixer and place it in a container. Cover the dough with a kitchen towel or plastic shower cap. Set the dough in a warm place (78 degrees-80 degrees F) for about 4 hours. The dough will puff up and look like it’s risen a bit by the end of 4 hours. If you want a more sour flavor in your monkey bread, you can let the dough ferment another hour or two.

Cold Bulk Fermentation

Place the covered dough in the refrigerator overnight for a cold bulk fermentation. This dough can stay in the refrigerator for up to 48 hours. I like using a cold bulk fermentation because it allows me to plan out my bakes better and adds more flavor to the dough. If you prefer to bake the monkey bread the same day, skip the cold bulk fermentation and move straight to shaping the dough.

Prepare the Pan and Brown Sugar Mixture

Before you divide and shape the sourdough monkey bread, prepare a bundt pan. This recipe uses a bundt pan for a unique and fun shape. You can use any pan you want if you don’t have a bundt pan. Melt the butter for the topping. Use a pastry brush to thoroughly spread melted butter into all the crevices to thoroughly coat the bundt pan. After the pan is prepared, mix the brown sugar/cinnamon/salt together.

Shaping Sourdough Monkey Bread

Turn the dough out of the container. It will be cold but as you work with it, it will warm up a bit. Using a bench scraper or sharp knife to cut the monkey bread into 8 sections. Cut each section of monkey bread into 6-8 pieces (depending on how large you like the pieces). You will end up with about 50-60 pieces of monkey bread. Roll each piece into a ball shape with your fingers and then dunk into the butter and then the topping mixture. Coat each ball completely in the mixture and place in the bundt pan. Continue layering the balls on top of each other until all the balls of dough are covered and the bundt pan is filled up with monkey bread bites. Pour any leftover butter and topping over the top of the monkey bread.

Proofing Sourdough Monkey Bread

Cover and let the monkey bread rest in a warm place for about 3 hours. I set my bread proofer to 82 degrees F which is a little warmer than usual. This helps warm up cold dough from being in the refrigerator a little more quickly. If you don’t have a bread proofer, use your oven with the light on to monitor the temperature of your dough. After about 3 hours, gently touch a dough ball. It should feel airy and light (no longer cold at all). If you press in on the dough ball it should spring back just a little bit. The dough should have puffed up but won’t necessarily rise to fill the bundt pan. If your dough is showing all of these signs, go ahead and preheat your oven to 350 degrees F. If it’s not showing these signs, let it continue rising for another half hour to hour. If you want more sour flavor, leave the dough to ferment even longer–another hour or two.

Baking Sourdough Monkey Bread

Put the sourdough monkey bread in a preheated 350 degree F oven and bake for 30-35 minutes. The monkey bread will puff up while it bakes and the brown sugar/cinnamon mixture will make a delicious coating and gooey sauce all over the monkey bread. After about 30 minutes, pull the sourdough monkey bread out of the oven and let it rest for about 5-10 minutes before turning it out onto a large plate. If you have trouble with the monkey bread not holding its shape, let it sit a little longer in the pan. Whisk together powdered sugar and whole milk and drizzle over the top of the warm sourdough monkey bread. Enjoy warm!

no:
Timing: This recipe takes a couple of days, start to finish. The hands on time is minimal but there is a lot of rising/resting/refrigerated time needed. Use my sample schedule in the post to help gauge the timing and keep the dough temperature at or slightly above 78 degrees F. You can make this all in one day if you mix a 1:1:1 levain in the morning, mix and let the dough rise for about 4 hours, then shape into monkey bread and let rise again for another 3-4 hours in warm 78 degree F place.

Bread Flour: I prefer using bread flour in recipes that knead the dough to develop the gluten. The result is a light and springy texture. If you don’t have bread flour, you can substitute all purpose flour.

If your peppers don't sit upright on your cutting board, trim about 1/8-inch off the bottoms to even them out so they can stand without falling over. Cut the top off each pepper about 1/2-inch down. Remove and discard the stems, then finely chop the remaining flesh from the tops. Scoop out the seeds and as much of the membranes as you can. Place the peppers in a large microwave-safe bowl with 1/2 cup water. Cover with plastic wrap and microwave on high power for 12 minutes. Carefully uncover and let them sit until ready to assemble.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Spread the beef in an even layer and cook undisturbed until lightly browned, about 3 minutes. Toss and continue to cook, breaking up any clumps with the back of a spoon and scraping up any browned bits from the pan until the meat is lightly browned all over, 6 to 8 minutes. Transfer the browned meat to a large bowl with a slotted spoon.

Reduce the heat to medium. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and add the reserved chopped peppers, onions, garlic, thyme, 4 teaspoons salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender but not browned, 10 to 12 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until falling apart and much of the liquid has evaporated, about 7 minutes.

Stir in the tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly until brick red colored, about 1 minute. Stir in the wine and cook until the mixture is reduced, very thick and no smell of alcohol remains, 6 to 8 minutes. Add the broth and bring to a boil. Transfer to the bowl with the beef. Stir in the rice until completely combined. (The mixture will be wet.) Season with salt and pepper.

Arrange a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 450 degrees F.

Place the peppers cut-side up in a 13-by-9-inch baking dish. Spoon the filling into the peppers, gently pressing it in with the back of a spoon. Be careful not to overstuff and split the sides of the peppers. Bake for 15 minutes. Then top with the cheese and continue baking until the filling is heated through and the cheese is browned in spots, 10 to 12 minutes.

d:
Marinade Instructions
 1. In a large bowl or container, whisk all marinade ingredients together until smooth.
 2. Add chicken tenders and toss to coat thoroughly.
 3. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight (up to 18 hours).
 4. Do not rinse or dry the chicken before dredging.

Dredging Instructions
 1. Mix all dredge ingredients together in a large bowl or tray.
 2. Remove chicken from marinade (no need to shake off).
 3. First dredge: Press chicken into flour mix, coating thoroughly. Shake off excess.
 4. Dip again briefly into the marinade.
 5. Second dredge: Press back into dredge again for craggy, crisp texture.
 6. Place coated tenders on a wire rack and let rest 15–20 minutes before frying.

Cooking Instructions

Deep Fryer Method
 1. Heat oil (peanut, canola, or soybean) to 350–365°F.
 2. Fry in batches, 5–6 minutes each, until golden brown and internal temp reaches 165°F.
 3. Drain on a wire rack.
 4. Immediately season with kosher or Maldon salt.

Air Fryer Method (Optional)
 1. Preheat to 400°F.
 2. Spray tenders and basket with oil.
 3. Air fry in batches for 10–12 minutes, flipping and re-spraying halfway through.
 4. Season with flaky salt while hot.

d:
PREPARE THE SOFFRITTO!

Heat olive oil in a large pan/pot on low-to-medium heat.

Add the onions, carrots, celery (and leaves) to the oil. Saute' until tender and somewhat translucent, and aromatic . . . for about 5 minutes

Although not part of a soffritto, for this recipe, add the minced garlic to the soffritto and saute' for another 3 minutes. Adding garlic at the end helps prevent it from burning.

When finished sauteeing, remove all of this from the pan and set it aside to use later on in the recipe.

FOR THE BOLOGNESE RAGU:

Add the pancetta to a medium-hot pan (it's ok to use the same pot/pan) and cooki until it is a reddish-brown color (about 10 minues), being careful not to burn the pancetta. It is fine to substitute guanciale or thick bacon.

When pancetta (or guanciale) is finished cooking, add all of the meats to the pan and begin to saute on low to medium heat. Break up all of the clumps of meat into a 'minced', ground meat texture. Mix the meats together thoroughly. For about 15 minutes, stir occasionally, and continue to break down any clumps.

At this time, I add seasonings that I believe enhance any recipe: Accent, Nature's Seasons, and Mrs. Dash Original Flavor Seasons. I sprinkle a good amout all over the meats.

When the meats are a nice brown color, add the soffritto (plus garlic) back into the cooked meats and mix everything thoroughly.

Add the herbs and the ground nutmeg, the lemon peel, and the Parmigiano rind.

Add the dry white wine and stir until well absorbed.

Add chicken broth one or two cups at a time, stir and allow it to be well-absorbed before adding the next round of chicken broth. Always add broth first and allow to fully absorbed after every addition of broth.

Add the cream and milk.

Add the freshly-grated Parmigiano cheese. You can add more later if you prefer.

Set the heat on low and simmer the Bolognese ragu for 2 - 3 hours, preferably 3 hours. Keep your eyes on it and stir occassionally so that the sauce does not burn. Also use a spoon to skim off any grease/fat that rises to the surface of the ragu while cooking; this will happen more near the end of cooking.

Add salt and pepper to taste. Add any more ingredients you feel you prefer, such as more Parmigiano cheese, more herbs and/or nutmget, more cream, more broth, etc.

Serve with wide, large pasta noodles that have been cooked al dente. Add pasta water to the sauce to achieve a more silky desired consistency. Serve on top of the pasta, or serve thoroughly 'mixed into' the pasta with extra sauce served and passed around to guests who want more sauce.

i: 1 lb deli roast beef, thinly sliced
d:
Make the jus: in a saucepan, combine the beef broth, Worcestershire, soy sauce, onion powder and butter. Bring to a simmer and cook 5 minutes.

Heat the broiler and set a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Split the rolls and set them open on a sheet pan.

Turn the jus down to low. Add the roast beef a handful at a time and let it warm in the jus for about 1 minute, then lift it out with tongs, letting the extra drip off.

Pile the beef onto the rolls and top each with 2 slices of Swiss.

Broil 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely, until the cheese melts and the bread toasts. Pour the remaining jus into small cups for dipping.
de: Shaved roast beef and Swiss with a quick au jus for dipping.

d:
Chop the rotisserie chicken into bite-size pieces, halve the grapes, and finely dice the celery.

In a large bowl, stir the mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, lemon juice and garlic powder together until smooth.

Fold in the chicken, grapes and celery. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Chill 15 minutes if you have time; the flavors come together.

Split the croissants horizontally. Warm them in a 350°F oven for 3 minutes if you like them crisp.

Line each croissant with a lettuce leaf and fill with a generous scoop of chicken salad.
de: Creamy chicken salad with grapes and celery on buttery croissants.

d:
Gently roll the beef into 8 loose balls (about 3 oz each); don't pack them tightly. Keep them in the fridge until the griddle is hot.

Make the sauce: stir the mayonnaise, mustard and relish together.

Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast them on the griddle or in a skillet until golden. Set aside.

Heat a griddle or cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Add 2 to 4 balls, top each with a few onion slices, and press firmly with a sturdy spatula into thin patties. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook about 2 minutes, until the edges are deeply browned and crispy. Scrape under each patty, flip, add a slice of cheese, and cook 1 minute more. Stack 2 patties on each bun with sauce and pickles.
de: Crispy-edged diner burgers on the Blackstone or a cast iron pan.

d:
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring now and then, about 15 minutes until soft and golden. Move to a plate and wipe out the skillet.

Shape the beef into 4 thin oval patties about the size of the bread. Season both sides with the seasoned salt.

Cook the patties in the skillet over medium-high heat about 2 minutes per side, until well browned but still a little pink in the middle. Move to a plate; they finish cooking in the sandwich.

Build each sandwich: rye bread, a slice of Swiss, a patty, a pile of onions, another slice of Swiss and a second slice of bread. Butter the outsides with the remaining butter.

Wipe the skillet and cook the sandwiches over medium-low heat 4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until the bread is crisp, the cheese is melted and the patties reach 160°F. A smear of Dijon or Thousand Island inside adds a nice tang.
de: Burger patties with caramelized onions and Swiss on griddled rye.

d:
Lay out the bread and spread pesto on one side of each slice.

On half the slices, layer the turkey, mozzarella and a handful of spinach, then close the sandwiches with the remaining slices, pesto side in.

Spread the outsides with the softened butter.

Heat a panini press, or a skillet over medium heat. If using a skillet, set a heavy pan on top of the sandwiches to press them.

Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, until the bread is golden and crisp and the mozzarella is melted. Slice and serve warm.

Ciabatta rolls work too; split them and press a little longer.
de: Turkey, mozzarella and pesto pressed until crispy.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil or parchment.

In a bowl, toss the chicken thighs with the olive oil, cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, garlic powder, half the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt until well coated.

Spread the chicken on the pan and roast 18 to 20 minutes, until browned at the edges and cooked through (175°F for thighs). Or grill over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes per side. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly.

While the chicken cooks, stir the yogurt with the minced garlic, the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt.

Warm the flatbreads. Fill each with lettuce, cucumber, sliced chicken and a spoonful of garlic yogurt sauce, then roll up.

Naan works in place of the flatbreads.
de: Warm-spiced chicken thighs with garlic yogurt sauce in wraps.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 baking dish.

Warm the frozen meatballs in the microwave for 3 to 4 minutes (or in the oven as the package directs) until hot, then cut each in half.

Without separating them, slice the slab of rolls in half horizontally. Set the bottom half in the dish and spread it with the Alfredo sauce.

Arrange the meatball halves cut-side down over the sauce and cover evenly with the mozzarella. Replace the tops.

Stir the melted butter with the garlic powder and parsley and brush it over the tops. Bake 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the tops are golden. Cut into sliders.
de: Frozen meatballs baked in Hawaiian rolls with garlic Alfredo and mozzarella.

i: 1 can (8 oz) pineapple rings, drained and quartered
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 baking dish.

In a saucepan or microwave-safe bowl, warm the shredded chicken with the teriyaki sauce, stirring until it's glossy and hot.

Without separating them, slice the slab of rolls in half horizontally. Set the bottom half in the dish and layer on half the Swiss, the teriyaki chicken, the pineapple pieces and the rest of the Swiss. Replace the tops.

Brush the tops with the melted butter and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.

Cover with foil and bake 12 minutes, then uncover and bake 3 minutes more to toast the tops. Cut into sliders.
de: Sweet teriyaki chicken with pineapple and Swiss on Hawaiian rolls.

d:
Put the eggs in a saucepan in a single layer and cover with cold water by 1 inch. Bring to a boil over high heat.

As soon as it boils, cover the pan, turn off the heat, and let the eggs sit 11 minutes. Move them to a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes, then peel.

Chop the eggs and put them in a bowl. Add the mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, relish, Dijon, celery, chives and paprika and stir gently. The yogurt lightens it and adds protein; the relish adds the tang it needs. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Toast the bread if you like. Spread the egg salad on half the slices, top with lettuce, and close the sandwiches.
de: Creamy egg salad on soft bread. Boil the eggs ahead to save time.
nu:
Calories: 390
Protein: 22g
Carbohydrate: 27g
Fat: 21g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

i: 2 cups frozen diced hash brown potatoes
d:
In a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, cook the sausage 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into crumbles, until browned. Move it to a bowl, leaving the drippings in the pan.

Add the frozen hash browns to the drippings in an even layer. Cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring only every few minutes, until golden and crisp. Season with salt and add them to the sausage.

Whisk the eggs with the milk, ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper. Lower the heat to medium-low, pour the eggs into the skillet, and stir slowly until softly set, 3 to 4 minutes.

Warm the tortillas for 20 seconds in the microwave so they fold without tearing. Fill each with eggs, sausage and potatoes, and a handful of cheddar. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.

Wipe out the skillet and toast the burritos seam-side down over medium heat 2 minutes per side, until golden. Serve with salsa verde or sour cream.
de: Sausage, eggs, potatoes and cheese. They freeze well.

d:
Heat the oven to the temperature on the biscuit package (usually 350°F). Lay the bacon on a foil-lined sheet pan.

Bake the biscuits per the package, 13 to 17 minutes. At the same time, bake the bacon 15 to 18 minutes until crisp. Drain the bacon on paper towels.

Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs (in batches) and fry 3 minutes, flipping once, or scramble them softly. Season with salt and pepper.

Split the warm biscuits. Fill each with an egg, a slice of cheddar and a slice of bacon broken in half; the heat of the egg melts the cheese.
de: Flaky biscuits stacked with bacon, egg and cheddar.

d:
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook about 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Pour in the chicken broth and add the thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 10 minutes, until the carrots are just tender.

Add the egg noodles and simmer 7 minutes, until tender.

Stir in the shredded chicken and parsley and heat through, 2 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper to taste. The noodles keep soaking up broth, so add a splash more broth to leftovers.
de: The classic. Rotisserie chicken makes it weeknight fast.

n: Creamy Chicken and Wild Rice Soup
d:
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes, until softened.

Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for 1 minute so it cooks without browning.

Slowly whisk in the chicken broth so no lumps form. Add the wild rice blend and thyme. Bring to a boil, then cover, lower the heat, and simmer 25 minutes (or the time on the rice package) until the rice is tender.

Stir in the shredded chicken and the cream and heat through over low heat, about 5 minutes; don't let it boil.

Season with salt and pepper to taste. If the soup thickens too much, stir in a little more broth.
de: Panera-style creamy soup with a wild rice blend.

d:
In a large pot over medium-high heat, brown the ground beef with the onion, about 7 minutes, breaking up the meat. Drain the fat and move the beef to a bowl.

Melt the butter in the same pot over medium heat. Add the carrots and celery and cook 4 minutes. Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the chicken broth until smooth. Add the potatoes and bring to a boil, then simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when poked with a fork.

Lower the heat. Stir in the milk and the beef, then add the cheddar a handful at a time, stirring until melted. Don't let it boil once the cheese is in.

Turn off the heat and stir in the sour cream. Season with salt and pepper. Top bowls with extra cheddar or diced pickles, like a cheeseburger.
de: Ground beef, potatoes and a velvety cheddar broth.

d:
In a large pot over medium-high heat, cook the sausage and onion 6 to 8 minutes, breaking the sausage into crumbles, until browned. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.

Add the chicken broth and Italian seasoning, scraping up the browned bits, and bring to a boil.

Add the tortellini and cook 5 minutes (or per the package), until they float and are tender.

Lower the heat and stir in the cream and parmesan. Add the spinach and stir until it wilts, about 1 minute.

Season with salt and pepper and serve with extra parmesan and crusty bread.
de: Italian sausage, cheese tortellini and spinach in a creamy, tomato-free broth.

d:
Heat the oven and bake the biscuits per the package so they're ready when the soup is.

Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes, until soft. Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the chicken broth until smooth. Add the potatoes and thyme, bring to a boil, then simmer 12 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.

Stir in the peas, chicken and cream and simmer gently 3 to 4 minutes, until everything is hot and the soup is creamy.

Season with salt and pepper. Ladle into bowls and top each with a split biscuit, like a pot pie crust.
de: All the pot pie flavor, served with flaky biscuits for dunking.

d:
In a large pot over medium heat, cook the chopped bacon 6 to 8 minutes, until crisp. Leave the bacon and its fat in the pot.

Add the onion and celery and cook 5 minutes, until soft. Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the chicken broth. Add the potatoes, bring to a boil, then simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.

Stir in the corn, ham and half and half. Simmer gently 5 minutes, until the corn is hot; don't let it boil hard.

Season with salt and pepper. Serve topped with the shredded cheddar.
de: A good way to use leftover ham.

i: 2 cans (15 oz) great northern beans, drained
tortilla chips and shredded cheese for topping
d:
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 4 minutes, until softened.

Add the chicken broth, drained beans, green chiles, corn and taco seasoning. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes.

Lower the heat, add the cubed cream cheese, and stir until it melts completely into the soup, 2 to 3 minutes.

Stir in the shredded chicken and heat through 3 minutes. Taste and add salt if needed.

Ladle into bowls and top with crushed tortilla chips and shredded cheese. Sour cream and avocado are good too.
de: Taco soup without tomatoes: white beans, corn and cream cheese.

n: Chicken and Corn Egg Drop Soup
d:
In a large pot, bring the chicken broth, soy sauce, ginger and frozen corn to a simmer over medium-high heat. Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer 3 minutes.

Stir the cornstarch into the water until smooth, then stir it into the simmering soup. Cook 2 minutes, stirring, until it thickens slightly and turns glossy.

Beat the eggs well in a measuring cup with a spout. Turn the heat to low so the soup is barely bubbling. While stirring slowly in one direction, pour the eggs in a thin stream; they set into silky ribbons within seconds.

Turn off the heat. Stir in the green onions and sesame oil. Taste and add salt and a pinch of pepper (white pepper is traditional); it should taste savory, not flat.

Serve with frozen potstickers or leftover rice to round it out. Chili crisp on top is the grown-up finisher.
de: The takeout favorite made a meal: silky egg ribbons, chicken and sweet corn in a gingery broth.
nu:
Calories: 260
Protein: 27g
Carbohydrate: 17g
Fat: 9g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

d:
In a large pot, combine the chicken broth, soy sauce, ginger and garlic. Bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes so the garlic softens.

Add the frozen wontons straight from the bag and return to a gentle boil. Cook about 5 minutes (or per the package), until they float and the filling is hot.

Add the chopped bok choy and shredded carrots for the last 2 minutes, until the bok choy stems are crisp-tender.

Turn off the heat, stir in the green onions and sesame oil, and taste for salt. Ladle into bowls with 5 or 6 wontons each.

Chicken wontons work the same way.
de: Frozen wontons and bok choy in a gingery broth.

d:
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes, until softened. Cut the frozen meatballs in half while the vegetables cook.

Add the chicken broth and bring to a boil.

Drop in the meatballs and the pasta. Lower to a steady simmer and cook 10 minutes, stirring now and then so the pasta doesn't stick, until the pasta is tender and the meatballs are hot through.

Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the parmesan. Season with salt and pepper, add a squeeze of lemon if you have one, and serve with extra parmesan. Acini di pepe is the traditional pasta if your store has it.
de: Mini meatballs, tiny pasta and spinach in chicken broth.
nu:
Calories: 430
Protein: 28g
Carbohydrate: 28g
Fat: 22g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

n: White Bean, Sausage and Kale Soup
d:
In a large pot over medium-high heat, cook the sausage with the onion and carrots 8 minutes, breaking up the sausage, until browned. Spoon off extra fat.

Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds. Add the broth, beans and Italian seasoning, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes.

Mash about a cup of the beans against the side of the pot with a spoon; this makes the soup creamier without cream.

Add the kale and simmer 5 minutes, until tender. Stir in the lemon juice, then season with salt and pepper; the lemon is what makes it taste finished. Top each bowl with parmesan. Chicken sausage works in place of pork sausage.
de: A hearty Tuscan-style soup with no tomatoes.

d:
In a large pot over medium-high heat, cook the sausage and onion 6 to 8 minutes, breaking up the sausage, until browned. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.

Add the chicken broth and Italian seasoning and bring to a boil. Add the broken lasagna noodles and cook 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often so they don't clump, until tender.

Lower the heat to medium-low. Stir in the cream, mozzarella and parmesan until the cheese melts. Add the spinach and stir until wilted.

Season with salt and pepper. Serve each bowl topped with a spoonful of ricotta, which melts in as you eat.
de: Lasagna in soup form with a creamy ricotta-parmesan broth instead of tomato.

i: 1 1/2 lb beef stew meat, cut small
d:
Pat the beef dry and season with 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in two batches, 4 to 5 minutes per batch. Move to a plate.

Add the onion, carrots, celery and mushrooms to the pot and cook 5 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.

Return the beef with any juices. Add the beef broth, barley, thyme and Worcestershire and bring to a boil.

Cover, lower the heat, and simmer 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the barley is plump and the beef is tender.

Season with salt and pepper. The barley keeps absorbing broth, so thin leftovers with a little water or broth.
de: Cozy and filling. Most of the time is hands-off simmering.

d:
In a large pot over medium heat, cook the chopped bacon 6 to 8 minutes until crisp. Lift it out with a slotted spoon, leaving the drippings.

Add the onion to the drippings and cook 4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.

Add the cauliflower and chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 minutes, until the cauliflower is very soft.

Blend with an immersion blender until mostly smooth (or blend half in a blender and stir it back in for a chunkier soup).

Over low heat, stir in the milk and cheddar until melted. Season with salt and pepper and top with sour cream, the bacon and green onions.
de: Tastes like loaded baked potato soup but is lighter.

i: 1 bag (30 oz) frozen diced hash brown potatoes
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Put the frozen hash browns, chicken broth, onion and cream of chicken soup in the slow cooker and stir.

Cover and cook on low 6 hours or high 3 hours, until the potatoes and onion are very tender.

Stir in the cubed cream cheese and cover for 10 minutes, then stir until it melts smoothly into the soup. Mash some of the potatoes against the side for a thicker soup.

Season with salt and pepper. Serve topped with cheddar, bacon and green onions.
de: A dump-and-go soup made with frozen hash browns.

d:
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Add the chicken broth and Alfredo sauce and whisk until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Add the tortellini and broccoli and simmer 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pasta is tender and the broccoli is bright green.

Stir in the chicken and parmesan and heat through, 2 minutes. Season with pepper and serve.
de: Creamy Alfredo soup with tortellini and broccoli.

d:
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 4 minutes, until soft.

Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the beef broth so no lumps form.

Add the Worcestershire, nutmeg and frozen meatballs. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes, until the meatballs are hot through.

Add the egg noodles and cook 7 minutes, until tender.

Turn off the heat and stir in the sour cream and parsley (stirring it in off the heat keeps it from curdling). Season with salt and pepper.
de: Frozen meatballs and egg noodles in a creamy beef broth.

i: shredded Monterey Jack cheese and sour cream for topping
d:
In a large pot over medium-high heat, cook the turkey and onion 7 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and cook 1 minute.

Add the salsa verde, chicken broth, beans and green chiles. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.

Simmer 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened. Mash some beans against the pot to thicken it more.

Season with salt. Serve topped with Monterey Jack and sour cream. Salsa verde is mild; pass hot sauce at the table for the adults.
de: A lean, mild green chili with ground turkey and white beans.

n: Chicken Caesar Salad with Garlic Croutons
d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Toss the bread cubes with the melted butter, garlic powder and a pinch of salt, spread on a sheet pan, and bake 8 to 10 minutes, tossing once, until golden and crisp.

Pound the chicken to an even ¾ inch if the breasts are thick. Rub with the oil and season with salt and pepper.

Cook the chicken in a skillet over medium-high heat 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

Make the dressing: whisk the mayonnaise, grated parmesan, lemon juice, Dijon, garlic and pepper with 1 to 2 tbsp water until pourable. Taste; it should be tangy and garlicky. Bottled Caesar usually contains anchovies, so this keeps it seafood-free.

Toss the romaine with the dressing until every leaf is coated. Top with the sliced chicken, croutons and shaved parmesan.
de: Crisp romaine, parmesan, homemade croutons and grilled chicken.
nu:
Calories: 610
Protein: 47g
Carbohydrate: 19g
Fat: 38g
Serving Size: 1 of 4 servings

d:
Warm the shredded chicken with the BBQ sauce in a skillet over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes, until hot and glossy.

Stir the ranch together with 1 tablespoon of BBQ sauce to make a BBQ ranch dressing.

Arrange the romaine on a platter or in bowls. Top with rows of corn, black beans, cheddar and tomatoes.

Add the BBQ chicken, drizzle with the BBQ ranch, and scatter the crispy fried onions on top just before serving so they stay crunchy.
de: Smoky BBQ chicken, corn, black beans and ranch over chopped romaine.

d:
Cook the rotini in salted water 1 minute longer than the package says. Drain, rinse with cold water until cool, and drain very well.

If the bacon isn't cooked yet, cook it until crisp, drain, and crumble.

In a large bowl, stir the ranch and sour cream together.

Add the pasta, chicken, bacon, cheddar, peas and green onions and toss until everything is coated. Season with salt and pepper.

Chill at least 10 minutes. It keeps up to 2 days; stir in a splash of ranch before serving if it has soaked up the dressing.
de: A cold pasta salad that holds up for lunches.

d:
In a large bowl, combine the coleslaw mix, romaine, shredded chicken, edamame, carrots and drained mandarin oranges.

Pour the sesame ginger dressing over the salad and toss well.

Let it sit 5 minutes so the cabbage softens slightly.

Top with the wonton strips and almonds right before serving so they stay crunchy.
de: Cabbage, carrots, edamame and crunchy wonton strips with sesame dressing.

d:
Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, about 7 minutes, breaking it up. Drain the fat.

Stir in the taco seasoning and water and simmer 5 minutes, until the liquid has mostly cooked off.

Stir the sour cream and ranch together for a creamy dressing.

Divide the romaine among bowls. Top with the warm beef, black beans, cheddar, avocado, tomatoes and crushed chips.

Drizzle with the dressing and serve right away. Add salsa at the table for anyone who wants it.
de: Seasoned beef over lettuce with cheese, beans and crushed tortilla chips.

d:
Cook the orzo in salted boiling water per the package, about 9 minutes. Drain, rinse with cold water, and drain well.

In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, oregano, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper.

Add the orzo and toss to coat. Add the chicken, cucumber, tomatoes, red onion and feta and toss again.

Taste and add salt or lemon. Serve right away or chill; it tastes even better after an hour in the fridge.
de: Orzo, cucumber, feta and chicken in a lemon-oregano vinaigrette.

d:
Season the chicken tenders with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tenders 3 to 4 minutes per side, until cooked through (165°F).

Set aside a few plain tenders for the kids. Toss the rest with the buffalo sauce in a bowl.

Divide the romaine, celery and carrots among plates.

Slice the tenders and lay them on the salads. Top with cheddar and drizzle with ranch. Blue cheese dressing is the grown-up swap.
de: Crispy buffalo chicken over greens with celery, carrots and blue cheese or ranch.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes with the oil, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper and roast cut-side down 25 minutes, until golden and tender.

Pat the steak dry and season well with salt and pepper. Let it sit while the potatoes roast.

Heat a heavy skillet over high heat until smoking. Sear the steak 4 to 5 minutes per side for medium (135°F). Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.

Divide the greens among plates. Top with potatoes, steak, tomatoes and cheese.

Drizzle with ranch and scatter the fried onions on top.

Crumbled blue cheese on the adults' plates is a good swap for the cheddar.
de: Seared steak, crispy roasted potatoes and greens with a creamy dressing.

d:
Rinse the quinoa in a fine strainer, then cook it per the package (usually 1 cup quinoa to 2 cups water, simmered 15 minutes). Fluff and let cool 10 minutes.

Whisk the olive oil, lime juice, cumin, ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper.

In a large bowl, combine the quinoa, chicken, beans, corn and bell pepper. Pour the dressing over and toss.

Fold in the avocado and cilantro gently so the avocado doesn't mash. Serve at room temperature or chilled.
de: Protein-packed quinoa with black beans, corn and a lime-cumin dressing.

d:
Pound the chicken to an even ¾ inch if thick. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side, until cooked through (165°F). Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

Arrange the spinach on plates with the strawberries, candied pecans and feta.

Top with the sliced chicken and drizzle with poppyseed dressing.
de: Spinach, strawberries, chicken, pecans and poppyseed dressing.

d:
Cook the rotini in salted water per the package. Drain, rinse with cold water, and drain well.

In a large bowl, combine the pasta, salami, ham, chickpeas, mozzarella pearls, tomatoes, cucumber and olives.

Pour the Italian dressing over and toss. Add the parmesan and toss again.

Chill at least 30 minutes so the pasta soaks up the dressing. Stir in a splash more dressing before serving if it looks dry.
de: Tri-color rotini with salami, mozzarella pearls and Italian dressing.
nu:
Calories: 640
Protein: 30g
Carbohydrate: 70g
Fat: 27g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

d:
In a bowl, stir the Greek yogurt and mayonnaise together with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Add the chicken, diced apple, celery, cranberries and pecans and fold until coated.

Separate the butter lettuce into cups, rinse, and pat dry.

Spoon the chicken salad into the lettuce cups and serve.
de: Crunchy, light and no cooking.

d:
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Cook in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes per side, until cooked through (165°F). Rest 5 minutes and slice.

Make the dressing: whisk the olive oil, apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon and a pinch of salt.

Slice the apples thinly just before serving so they don't brown.

Toss the greens with half the dressing. Top with the apples, cranberries, pecans, goat cheese and chicken, and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.
de: Fall salad with apples, cranberries, goat cheese and maple vinaigrette.

i: 1 bag (24 oz) frozen breaded chicken tenders
d:
Bake the frozen chicken tenders per the package until hot and crisp. Let them rest 2 minutes, then slice.

If you need hard-boiled eggs, cover eggs with water, bring to a boil, cover, turn off the heat for 11 minutes, then cool in ice water and peel.

Arrange the romaine on plates with rows of cheddar, sliced eggs, tomatoes and bacon.

Top with the sliced tenders and serve with honey mustard dressing.
de: Restaurant-style salad with crispy tenders and honey mustard.

i: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cubed
d:
Start the rice per the package. Steam the broccoli (microwave in a covered bowl with 2 tbsp water for 3 to 4 minutes) until bright green and crisp-tender.

Whisk the sauce: soy sauce, brown sugar, honey, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, cornstarch and ¼ cup water.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook 6 to 7 minutes, stirring once or twice, until browned and cooked through.

Pour in the sauce and stir. Simmer 2 minutes, until thick and glossy and coating the chicken.

Serve over rice with the broccoli, sprinkled with sesame seeds.
de: Sticky homemade teriyaki chicken with steamed broccoli over rice.

i: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and warmed
d:
Cook the rice per the package. Stir in the lime juice and cilantro once it's done.

Rub the chicken with the oil and taco seasoning on both sides.

Cook the chicken in a skillet over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes per side, until cooked through (165°F). Rest 5 minutes, then dice.

Warm the beans and corn together in a small pot or the microwave.

Build bowls with cilantro-lime rice, chicken, beans and corn, cheese, avocado and a spoonful of sour cream. Add salsa at the table.
de: Cilantro-lime rice, seasoned chicken, beans, corn and toppings.

d:
Whisk the pineapple juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, ketchup, garlic and ginger. Pour ½ cup into a small saucepan for basting and serving.

Put the chicken in a bag or dish with the remaining sauce and marinate at least 15 minutes, or up to overnight in the fridge.

Cook the rice. Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Simmer the reserved sauce 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thickened.

Grill the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side, brushing with the thickened sauce in the last few minutes, until cooked through (175°F). Grill the pineapple rings 2 minutes per side (fresh pineapple spears are even better if you have one).

Slice the chicken and serve over rice with grilled pineapple and green onions, with any leftover sauce on the side.
de: Hawaiian-style sweet and savory grilled chicken with pineapple and rice.

i: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cubed
d:
Start the rice per the package, and steam the broccoli until crisp-tender (green beans work too).

Whisk the honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, cornstarch and 2 tbsp water in a small bowl.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until browned and cooked through.

Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce and simmer 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until it's thick and coats the chicken.

Serve over rice with the vegetables, spooning extra sauce over the top.
de: Sweet and savory sauce kids love, all in one skillet.

d:
Use rice cooked a day ahead and chilled; it fries without getting mushy. Break up any clumps with your hands.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and cook 5 to 6 minutes, until cooked through. Move to a plate.

Pour in the eggs and scramble 1 minute until just set. Add them to the chicken.

Add the remaining oil, the onion and the peas and carrots. Cook 3 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the rice and spread it out. Let it sit 1 minute to toast, then stir and fry 3 to 4 minutes. Add the soy sauce, hoisin, chicken and eggs and toss well. Finish with sesame oil and green onions.
de: Faster and better than takeout. Use day-old rice.

d:
Start the rice. Toss the chicken with the cornstarch, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper until coated.

Whisk the sauce: soy sauce, hoisin, honey, rice vinegar and ¼ cup water.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.

Add the bell pepper, snap peas and garlic and stir-fry 2 minutes, until crisp-tender.

Pour in the sauce and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until thick and glossy. Stir in the cashews and serve over rice.
de: Tender chicken and toasted cashews in a savory brown sauce.

i: 1 can (20 oz) pineapple chunks, juice reserved
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and start the rice. Drain the pineapple, saving the juice.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper and toss it in the cornstarch until coated. Dip the pieces in the beaten eggs, letting the extra drip off.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken in batches 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden (it finishes in the oven). Move it to a 9x13 baking dish.

In a small saucepan, simmer the sugar, vinegar, ketchup, soy sauce and ½ cup of the pineapple juice 3 minutes, stirring until the sugar dissolves.

Scatter the bell pepper and pineapple over the chicken, pour the sauce over everything, and stir to coat. Bake 15 minutes, stirring once, until the sauce is bubbly and the chicken is cooked through. Serve over rice.
de: Crispy baked chicken in a sweet and sour sauce with pineapple and peppers.

i: 1 1/2 lb flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
d:
Start the rice. Slice the flank steak thinly against the grain (it's easier if you freeze it 20 minutes first). Pat dry and toss with the cornstarch until coated.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the beef in 2 or 3 batches, 2 to 3 minutes each, until browned and crisp at the edges. Move to a plate.

Pour off all but 1 tsp oil. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 30 seconds.

Add the soy sauce, brown sugar and water. Simmer 5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.

Return the beef, add the green onions, and toss 1 minute to glaze. Serve over rice.
de: Crispy flank steak in a sweet soy-garlic glaze.

d:
Melt the butter in a large deep skillet (one with a lid) over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper and cook it with the onion 5 minutes, until the chicken is no longer pink outside.

Stir in the rice for 1 minute so the grains are coated. Add the broth and garlic powder and bring to a boil.

Cover, turn the heat to low, and simmer 15 minutes without lifting the lid.

Scatter the broccoli over the top, cover again, and cook 5 minutes more, until the rice is tender and the broccoli is bright green.

Turn off the heat and stir in the cheddar and milk until creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
de: A one-pan comfort meal kids ask for again.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and start the basmati rice.

Toss the chicken thighs with the olive oil, cumin, paprika, turmeric, garlic powder, half the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt. Spread on a lined sheet pan.

Roast 20 minutes, until browned at the edges and cooked through (175°F). Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of the remaining lemon. Stir the yogurt with the minced garlic, the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.

Build bowls with rice, sliced chicken, the cucumber-tomato salad and a spoonful of garlic yogurt.
de: Spiced chicken, rice, cucumber-tomato salad and garlic sauce.

n: One-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with salt, pepper and half the oregano.

Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken 3 minutes per side until golden (it finishes in the oven). Move to a plate.

Add the onion to the skillet and cook 3 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then stir in the rice for 1 minute.

Add the broth, lemon zest and juice, thyme and the rest of the oregano, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a simmer and nestle the chicken on top.

Cover with a lid or foil and bake 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 175°F. Dot with butter, let stand 5 minutes, and fluff the rice.
de: Seared chicken thighs baked on lemony rice.

d:
Start the rice and steam the broccoli until crisp-tender.

Season the chicken with salt and toss it in the cornstarch until well coated.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken in a single layer, in batches if needed, 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Move to a plate.

Wipe out any burnt bits. Add the soy sauce, honey, brown sugar, rice vinegar, sesame oil and garlic to the skillet and simmer 2 minutes, until syrupy.

Return the chicken and toss to coat. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve over rice with the broccoli.
de: Crispy chicken bites in a sweet sesame glaze.

d:
Start the basmati rice.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and onion, season with salt, and cook 6 minutes until the chicken is lightly browned.

Add the garlic, curry powder and ginger and stir 1 minute, until fragrant.

Pour in the coconut milk, broth and honey. Simmer 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens slightly and the chicken is cooked through.

Stir in the spinach until wilted. Taste for salt and serve over rice. Curry powder labeled mild keeps it kid-friendly.
de: A creamy, mild yellow curry with coconut milk. Good for kids new to curry.

d:
In a large deep skillet or pot over medium-high heat, brown the sausage slices and ground meat 6 to 8 minutes, breaking up the meat.

Add the onion, bell pepper and celery and cook 5 minutes, until soft.

Stir in the garlic, Cajun seasoning and rice for 1 minute so the rice is coated.

Add the broth and bring to a boil. Cover, lower the heat, and simmer 18 minutes without lifting the lid.

Let stand 5 minutes, fluff with a fork, and stir in the green onions. Cajun seasoning is salty, so taste before adding salt.

Ground pork works in place of the beef.
de: Smoked sausage and rice with the Cajun trinity. Mild, with no tomatoes.

n: Ground Turkey and Zucchini Rice Skillet
d:
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and cook 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.

Add the zucchini, bell pepper, garlic and Italian seasoning. Cook 5 minutes, until the zucchini is tender but not mushy. Season with salt and pepper.

Stir in the cooked rice and parmesan and cook 2 minutes until hot.

Sprinkle the mozzarella over the top, cover, and cook on low 2 to 3 minutes until melted.
de: A lean, veggie-heavy skillet with a light garlic-parmesan finish.

d:
Use cold, day-old rice and break up any clumps.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set and move to a plate.

Add the remaining oil. Brown the ham and pineapple 4 minutes, until the pineapple caramelizes at the edges. Add the peas and carrots and cook 2 minutes.

Add the rice, spread it out, and let it sit 1 minute to toast. Stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes.

Add the soy sauce and eggs and toss well. Finish with sesame oil and green onions.
de: Hawaiian fried rice. Good for leftover ham.

d:
Cook the noodles per the package, drain, and toss with a few drops of the sesame oil so they don't stick.

Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, brown sugar and the rest of the sesame oil in a small bowl.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken 4 to 5 minutes, until cooked through.

Add the cabbage, carrots, snap peas and garlic and stir-fry 3 minutes, until crisp-tender.

Add the noodles and the sauce and toss over high heat for 2 minutes, until everything is coated and hot.

Spaghetti stands in fine for lo mein noodles.
de: Takeout-style noodles with chicken and vegetables.

d:
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and cook 5 to 6 minutes until cooked through. Move to a plate.

Scramble the eggs in the skillet until just set and add them to the chicken.

Add the remaining oil, the peas and carrots and the garlic. Cook 2 minutes.

Add the frozen riced cauliflower and cook 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the moisture cooks off and the cauliflower is tender.

Stir in the soy sauce, chicken and eggs. Finish with sesame oil and green onions.
de: Low-carb fried rice made with riced cauliflower.

d:
Start the instant brown rice per the package (about 10 minutes). Whisk the sauce: soy sauce, honey, ginger, cornstarch and ⅓ cup water.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and stir-fry 5 minutes, until cooked through. Move to a plate.

Add the remaining oil, the broccoli, bell pepper, snap peas and carrots. Stir-fry 4 minutes, until crisp-tender. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Return the chicken, stir the sauce, and pour it in. Simmer 1 minute, until glossy and thick. Serve over rice.
de: A light, colorful stir fry with a simple soy-ginger sauce.

d:
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for the fettuccine.

Pound the chicken to an even ¾ inch, season with salt and pepper, and cook in the olive oil over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes per side, until cooked through (165°F). Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

Cook the pasta per the package. Save 1 cup of pasta water before draining.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic for 1 minute. Pour in the cream and simmer gently 4 minutes, until slightly thickened.

Lower the heat and whisk in the parmesan a handful at a time until smooth. Toss with the pasta, adding pasta water a splash at a time until silky. Top with chicken and parsley.
de: Homemade Alfredo in the time it takes to boil the pasta.

d:
Cook the penne in salted water per the package and drain, saving ½ cup pasta water.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes, until browned and cooked through.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and garlic and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.

Pour in the broth and half and half and simmer 3 minutes.

Stir in the parmesan and Italian seasoning until smooth, then add the pasta and toss. Thin with pasta water if needed.
de: Bite-size chicken in a light garlic-butter parmesan sauce.

i: 1 box (10 oz) frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the lasagna noodles per the package, drain, and lay them flat on oiled foil so they don't stick.

In a bowl, mix the ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, the parmesan, egg, spinach (squeezed very dry), chicken, garlic powder and a pinch of salt and pepper.

Spread ½ cup Alfredo in the bottom of a 9x13 dish.

Spread about ⅓ cup filling along each noodle, roll it up from a short end, and set it seam-side down in the dish.

Spoon the remaining Alfredo over the rolls and sprinkle with the rest of the mozzarella. Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 minutes more until bubbly and golden.
de: Lasagna noodles rolled with ricotta and spinach and baked in Alfredo.

d:
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the spaghetti, adding the peas for the last minute. Before draining, save 1 cup of pasta water.

Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp. Move it to a plate, leaving 1 tbsp of the drippings.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper and cook it in the drippings 5 to 6 minutes until cooked through. Add the garlic for 30 seconds. Turn off the heat.

Whisk the eggs and parmesan in a bowl.

Add the hot drained pasta and peas to the skillet (heat off) and pour in the egg mixture, tossing quickly. Add pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is creamy, not scrambled. Toss in the bacon and serve right away.
de: Silky egg-and-parmesan sauce with bacon and chicken. No cream needed.

d:
Cook the rigatoni in salted water per the package. Save ½ cup pasta water and drain.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper and cook 6 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Move to a plate.

Add the mushrooms to the skillet in a single layer and cook 6 minutes without stirring too much, until browned. Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.

Pour in the broth, scraping up the browned bits, then the cream. Simmer 4 minutes until slightly thickened.

Stir in the parmesan until smooth. Add the chicken and pasta and toss, thinning with pasta water if needed. Season with salt and pepper.
de: Golden mushrooms and chicken in a garlic cream sauce.

d:
Cook the rotini in salted water per the package and drain.

In a large skillet over medium heat, cook the bacon until crisp. Move it to a plate and pour off all but 1 tbsp of the drippings.

Add the chicken to the skillet with half the ranch seasoning and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until cooked through.

Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the milk, cream cheese and the rest of the ranch seasoning and stir until the cream cheese melts into a smooth sauce, 3 minutes.

Stir in the cheddar until melted, then the pasta and most of the bacon. Top with the remaining bacon.
de: Creamy ranch pasta with bacon and cheddar.

d:
Cook the macaroni in salted water 1 minute less than the package says and drain.

In the same pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the milk until smooth. Simmer, whisking often, 4 minutes, until it coats a spoon.

Turn off the heat. Stir in the cheddar and Monterey Jack a handful at a time until melted, then the dry mustard and garlic powder. Season with salt.

Fold in the macaroni and serve right away. A splash of milk loosens leftovers when reheating.
de: Creamy homemade mac. Add ham, hot dogs or broccoli if you like.

d:
Cook the tortellini per the package and drain.

In the same pot over medium-low heat, warm the pesto and cream together until steaming, 2 minutes.

Add the chicken and spinach and stir until the spinach wilts and the chicken is hot.

Add the tortellini and parmesan and toss gently. Season with pepper and serve.
de: Cheese tortellini tossed with pesto cream, chicken and spinach.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 baking dish.

Cook the penne in salted water, adding the broccoli for the last 2 minutes. Drain well.

In a large bowl, stir together the pasta and broccoli, chicken, Alfredo, milk, garlic powder and 1 cup mozzarella.

Spread in the dish and top with the remaining mozzarella and the parmesan.

Bake uncovered 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbly and golden in spots. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
de: A baked penne Alfredo with chicken and broccoli under a mozzarella crust.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F. Cook the lasagna noodles per the package and lay them flat on oiled foil.

Make the white sauce: melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the broth and milk. Simmer 5 minutes until thick. Stir in the garlic powder, Italian seasoning and ½ cup parmesan, and season with salt and pepper.

Stir the ricotta and egg together in a bowl.

Spread ½ cup sauce in a 9x13 dish. Layer noodles, dollops of ricotta, chicken, spinach, mozzarella and more sauce. Repeat three times, ending with noodles, sauce, the remaining mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan.

Cover with foil and bake 40 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes before cutting so it holds together.
de: A creamy white lasagna with chicken, spinach and three cheeses.

d:
Cook the egg noodles per the package, drain, and toss with 1 tbsp butter. Heat the meatballs per the package.

Melt the remaining butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the beef broth, then the Worcestershire, Dijon and nutmeg. Simmer 5 minutes, until thick enough to coat a spoon.

Turn the heat to low and stir in the sour cream until smooth (don't let it boil). Add the meatballs and turn to coat.

Serve the meatballs and gravy over the buttered noodles.
de: Frozen meatballs in a creamy beef gravy over buttered noodles.

d:
In a large deep skillet over medium-high heat, brown the beef 7 minutes, breaking it up. Drain the fat.

Stir in the garlic powder, onion powder and paprika with ½ tsp salt.

Add the broth, milk and macaroni. Bring to a boil, then cover, lower the heat, and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every few minutes so the pasta doesn't stick, until the macaroni is tender.

Turn off the heat and stir in the cheddar and mustard until melted and creamy; the mustard gives it that cheeseburger tang. Let stand 2 minutes to thicken.
de: The boxed classic, made from scratch in one pot.
nu:
Calories: 520
Protein: 37g
Carbohydrate: 32g
Fat: 26g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

d:
Cook the penne in salted water per the package and drain.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 6 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Move to a plate.

Add the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes to the skillet and cook 1 minute.

Pour in the cream, broth and Italian seasoning. Simmer 4 minutes, until slightly thickened.

Stir in the parmesan until smooth, then the spinach until wilted. Add the chicken and pasta and toss.
de: Sun-dried tomato cream sauce with spinach and parmesan. It's creamy, not red.

d:
Cook the orecchiette in salted water, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Save 1 cup pasta water and drain.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the sausage 7 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned.

Add the garlic and cook 1 minute, until golden at the edges.

Add the pasta and broccoli, butter and parmesan. Toss over medium heat, adding pasta water a splash at a time, until the sauce is glossy and coats everything.
de: Italian sausage, broccoli, garlic and parmesan with no sauce needed.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 dish. Cook the spaghetti 2 minutes less than the package says and drain.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion 6 minutes, until soft and browned.

Stir in the flour for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth and milk and simmer 4 minutes, until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
