Combine the sauce with the spaghetti, chicken, peas and ¾ cup parmesan. Spread in the dish.

Top with the panko and the remaining parmesan. Bake 25 minutes, until bubbly and golden.
de: Spaghetti, chicken and mushrooms baked in a creamy sauce.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the ziti 2 minutes less than the package says and drain.

Brown the sausage in a skillet over medium-high heat 7 minutes, breaking it up. Drain any fat.

In a large bowl, combine the pasta, sausage, Alfredo, milk, Italian seasoning and 1 cup mozzarella.

Spread half in a 9x13 dish. Dollop the ricotta over it, then add the rest of the pasta.

Top with the remaining mozzarella and the parmesan. Bake 25 minutes, until bubbly and golden.
de: Baked ziti made with Alfredo, ricotta and Italian sausage.

i: 1 box (10 oz) frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the shells 2 minutes less than the package says, drain, and spread them on a sheet pan to cool slightly.

Squeeze the thawed spinach very dry in a towel. Mix it with the ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, the parmesan, egg, garlic powder and a pinch of salt.

Spoon about 2 tablespoons of filling into each shell.

Spread half the Alfredo in a 9x13 dish. Arrange the shells in it, open side up. Spoon the rest of the Alfredo over and sprinkle with the remaining mozzarella.

Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 5 minutes more until bubbly.
de: Jumbo shells stuffed with three cheeses and baked in garlic Alfredo.

n: Garlic Butter Steak Bites and Pasta
i: 1 1/2 lb sirloin steak, cut into 1-inch cubes
d:
Cook the penne in salted water per the package and drain, saving ½ cup pasta water.

Pat the steak cubes dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat until shimmering.

Sear the steak in batches, 2 to 3 minutes total, turning once, until browned outside and pink inside. Move to a plate.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and garlic and cook 1 minute. Stir in the cream and parmesan until smooth.

Add the pasta and steak with its juices and toss, adding pasta water if needed. Top with parsley.
de: Seared steak bites tossed with pasta in garlic butter and parmesan.

i: 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs, toasted in butter
d:
Cook the penne in salted water per the package and drain. Toast the panko in a small skillet with 1 tsp butter over medium heat, stirring, until golden, about 3 minutes.

Melt the 3 tbsp butter in a large pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the milk until smooth. Simmer 4 to 5 minutes, whisking often, until it coats a spoon.

Lower the heat and stir in the Dijon, then the Swiss a handful at a time until melted. Season with salt and pepper.

Add the chicken, ham and pasta and stir until hot. Serve topped with the toasted panko for crunch.
de: Chicken, ham and Swiss in a creamy Dijon sauce with crispy panko.

d:
Cook the cavatappi in salted water per the package and drain.

Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pepper and onion 6 minutes, until soft and browned at the edges.

Add the shaved beef and garlic, breaking the beef apart, and cook 3 to 4 minutes until browned. Season with salt and pepper.

Pour in the cream, broth and Worcestershire. Simmer 4 minutes, until slightly thickened.

Lower the heat and stir in the torn provolone until melted, then add the pasta and toss to coat.
de: Shaved steak, peppers and onions in a provolone cream sauce.

d:
Cook the linguine in salted water per the package and drain.

Season the flour with ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Dredge the chicken cutlets, shaking off the extra.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Move to a plate.

Add the remaining oil and the mushrooms and cook 5 minutes until browned. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the Marsala and broth, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer 5 minutes until reduced by about a third.

Stir in the cream and butter until glossy. Return the chicken to warm through 2 minutes, spooning sauce over it. Serve over the linguine.

No Marsala? Use another ¾ cup broth plus 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar for the same sweet-tart depth.
de: Restaurant-style creamy mushroom Marsala sauce over linguine.

d:
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil (you'll cook the angel hair at the very end; it only takes 3 minutes).

Season the flour with ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Dredge the cutlets and shake off the extra.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F inside. Move to a cutting board.

Lower the heat to medium. Melt the butter in the skillet with the garlic for 1 minute. Add the broth and lemon juice and simmer 4 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Meanwhile, drop the angel hair into the boiling water and cook about 3 minutes; save ½ cup pasta water and drain.

Toss the pasta in the sauce with the parmesan, adding pasta water if it looks dry. Taste for salt and lemon. Slice the chicken and lay it on top. Scatter capers over the adults' plates.
de: Bright lemon-butter sauce over angel hair. Capers are optional.

i: 1 box (16 oz) frozen potato and cheese pierogies
d:
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Boil the frozen pierogies 3 minutes, until they float, then drain well and pat dry.

Meanwhile, melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the kielbasa and onion 6 minutes, until the onion is soft and the sausage is browned. Push to one side.

Add the remaining butter to the empty side of the skillet. Add the pierogies in a single layer and brown 2 to 3 minutes per side.

Toss everything together and serve with sour cream and green onions.
de: Frozen pierogies and smoked sausage browned with onions in butter.

n: Garlic Butter Turkey Meatballs with Zucchini Noodles
i: Optional: 8 oz spaghetti, for the kids
d:
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.

In a bowl, gently mix the turkey, panko, egg, parmesan, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and ½ tsp salt. Roll into 1½-inch balls (wet hands help) and set on the pan.

Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until browned and cooked through (165°F).

While they bake, cook the spaghetti for the kids if using, and drain.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat with the minced garlic for 1 minute. Add the zucchini noodles and toss 2 minutes, just until warm (longer makes them watery). Add the meatballs, and serve the spaghetti tossed in some of the garlic butter for anyone who wants it.
de: Baked turkey meatballs over zoodles and pasta in garlic butter.

n: Cheesy Chicken Bacon Ranch Tater Tot Casserole
i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Heat the oven to 400°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

In a large bowl, mix the chicken, bacon, cream of chicken soup, sour cream, ranch seasoning and 1 cup cheddar.

Spread the mixture in the dish and cover it with the frozen tater tots in a single, snug layer.

Bake 35 minutes, until the tots are golden and crisp.

Sprinkle with the remaining cheddar and bake 5 minutes more, until melted. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
de: Ranch chicken and bacon under a crispy tater tot top.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F. Cook the rice if you don't have leftover rice.

Mix the chicken, cream of chicken soup, sour cream and half the poppy seeds. Spread in a greased 8x8 or 9x13 dish.

Toss the crushed crackers with the melted butter and the remaining poppy seeds, and scatter evenly over the top.

Bake 30 minutes, until bubbly at the edges and golden on top. Serve over rice.
de: Creamy chicken under a buttery Ritz cracker topping.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper 5 minutes, until soft.

Stir in both soups, the green chiles, sour cream, cumin and chili powder until smooth, then fold in the chicken.

Layer a third of the torn tortillas in the dish, then a third of the chicken mixture and a third of the cheese. Repeat twice more, ending with cheese.

Bake 30 minutes, until bubbly and golden. Let stand 10 minutes before cutting.
de: The Texas classic made with green chiles instead of Rotel.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F. Steam the broccoli 3 minutes (it finishes in the oven) and lay it in a greased 9x13 dish with the chicken on top.

Whisk the cream of chicken soup, Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, curry powder and 1 cup cheddar.

Spread the sauce evenly over the chicken and broccoli.

Toss the panko with the melted butter. Sprinkle the remaining cheddar and the panko over the top.

Bake 30 minutes, until bubbly and golden.
de: Chicken and broccoli in a lightened cheddar sauce.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
Optional: 1 can (4 oz) diced green chiles
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish. Cook the spaghetti in salted water 2 minutes less than the package says and drain.

In the same pot over medium-low heat, stir the soup, cubed Velveeta, broth, milk and garlic powder until the cheese melts and the sauce is smooth.

Add the chicken, green chiles if using, and the spaghetti, and toss until coated.

Spread in the dish, top with the cheddar, and bake 20 minutes, until bubbly.
de: Creamy chicken spaghetti with Velveeta and no Rotel.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F.

In a 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat, whisk the soup, broth, milk, thyme and garlic powder and bring to a simmer.

Stir in the chicken and frozen vegetables and simmer 3 minutes until hot. Season with salt and pepper.

Cut each biscuit into quarters and scatter them over the filling, leaving small gaps so steam can escape.

Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the biscuits are golden and cooked through in the center.
de: Creamy chicken and vegetables baked under fluffy biscuits.

i: 1 bag (30 oz) frozen shredded hash browns, thawed
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish. Thaw the hash browns and pat dry.

In a large bowl, mix the hash browns, ham, soup, sour cream, 1½ cups cheddar, onion and 2 tbsp melted butter.

Spread in the dish and sprinkle with the remaining cheddar.

Toss the crushed cornflakes with the remaining butter and scatter over the top.

Bake 45 minutes, until bubbly and golden. Let stand 5 minutes.
de: Cheesy hash brown casserole loaded with ham.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Stir together the chicken, frozen green beans, soup and sour cream and spread in the dish.

In a bowl, stir the stuffing mix with the hot broth and melted butter until moistened.

Spoon the stuffing evenly over the chicken mixture.

Bake 30 minutes, until the filling is bubbly and the stuffing is crisp on top.
de: A Thanksgiving-flavored weeknight bake with green beans.

i: 1 bag (9 oz) nacho cheese Doritos, crushed
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat and drain. Add the taco seasoning and ⅔ cup water and simmer 5 minutes.

Stir in the black beans, queso and sour cream until combined.

Spread half the crushed Doritos in the dish. Add the beef mixture and the shredded cheese. Top with the rest of the Doritos.

Bake 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted. Top with shredded lettuce (and tomatoes or salsa for the adults) and serve right away.
de: Taco beef, queso and crushed Doritos baked together.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish. Cook the egg noodles per the package and drain.

Brown the beef with the garlic powder and ½ tsp salt in a large skillet. Drain the fat and stir in the cream of mushroom soup.

In a large bowl, mix the softened cream cheese, sour cream and green onions until smooth, then fold in the noodles.

Spread half the noodles in the dish, add the beef mixture, then the rest of the noodles.

Top with the cheddar and bake 25 minutes, until bubbly and the cheese is melted.
de: Ground beef and egg noodles in a sour cream and cream cheese layer.

i: 2 boxes (16 oz) frozen potato and cheese pierogies
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Brown the kielbasa and onion 6 minutes.

Whisk the sour cream with the chicken broth until smooth.

Layer the frozen pierogies in the dish, scatter the kielbasa and onion over them, and pour the sauce over everything.

Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover, top with the cheddar and bacon, and bake 10 minutes more, until melted and bubbly.
de: Frozen pierogies baked with kielbasa, cheddar and a sour cream sauce.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the steak, pepper and onion 5 to 6 minutes, breaking up the steak, until browned. Season with salt and pepper.

In a large bowl, stir the soup and milk together. Add the steak mixture and the quartered biscuits and fold until the biscuits are coated.

Spread in the dish and bake 25 minutes, until the biscuits are puffed and cooked through in the center.

Top with the provolone and bake 5 minutes more, until melted.
de: Biscuit pieces baked with steak, peppers and provolone.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish. Cook the rice per the package.

In a large bowl, mix the cooked rice, chopped broccoli, chicken, soup, sour cream, milk and 2 cups cheddar. Season with salt and pepper.

Spread in the dish and sprinkle with the remaining cheddar.

Toss the crushed crackers with the melted butter and scatter over the top.

Bake 30 minutes, until bubbly and golden.
de: The classic baked rice casserole kids love.

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Whisk both soups with the chicken broth until smooth. Stir in the uncooked rice and pour it into the dish, spreading it evenly.

Lay the chicken on top and sprinkle with the dry onion soup mix and paprika.

Cover the dish tightly with foil (this is what cooks the rice) and bake 75 minutes without peeking.

Check that the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 175°F (thighs are juicier at this temperature). Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
de: Dump-and-bake chicken and rice. Ten minutes of work, then the oven does the rest.

i: 2 1/2 lb russet potatoes, sliced 1/8 inch thick
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup
d:
Heat the oven to 400°F and grease a 9x13 baking dish. Whisk the soup, milk, garlic powder, thyme, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper.

Layer half the potato slices and onion in the dish, pour on half the sauce and sprinkle with half the cheddar. Repeat. Cover tightly with foil and bake 35 minutes, until the potatoes are nearly tender when poked with a knife.

About 10 minutes before the potatoes are ready, pat the chops dry and season with salt and pepper. Sear in the oil in a hot skillet 2 minutes per side, just to brown them.

Uncover the potatoes, set the chops on top, and bake uncovered 15 to 20 minutes, until the chops reach 145°F and the potatoes are tender and golden at the edges.

Rest 5 minutes before serving. A spoonful of applesauce or a few pickles on the side cuts the richness.
de: Seared pork chops baked over creamy sliced potatoes.
nu:
Calories: 560
Protein: 42g
Carbohydrate: 44g
Fat: 23g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Season the chicken lightly with salt and pepper, lay it in the dish, and cover each piece with a slice of Swiss.

Whisk the soup with the milk and pour it over the chicken.

Sprinkle the stuffing mix evenly over the top and drizzle with the melted butter.

Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 minutes more, until the stuffing is crisp and the chicken reaches 165°F.
de: Chicken breasts baked under Swiss cheese, cream sauce and buttery stuffing.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Halve the zucchini lengthwise and scoop out the centers with a spoon, leaving a ¼-inch shell.

Chop the scooped zucchini and mix it with the chicken, Alfredo, Italian seasoning and a pinch of salt and pepper.

Set the boats in a baking dish and fill them with the chicken mixture.

Top with mozzarella and parmesan.

Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the zucchini is tender and the cheese is golden.
de: Zucchini halves stuffed with Alfredo chicken and mozzarella.

i: sour cream and salsa verde for dipping
d:
Toss the shredded chicken with the taco seasoning (add a splash of water if it seems dry).

Lay out the tortillas. On half of each, scatter cheese, chicken and a little more cheese, then fold over.

Melt a little butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook 2 quesadillas at a time, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts.

Let rest 1 minute, then cut into wedges. Serve with sour cream and salsa verde.
de: Crispy cheesy quesadillas. Good for leftover chicken.

i: 1 1/2 lb chicken breast, sliced into strips
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with foil.

On the pan, toss the chicken strips, peppers and onion with the oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, paprika and 1 tsp salt. Spread out in a single layer (use two pans if crowded).

Roast 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.

Switch to broil for 2 minutes to char the edges, watching closely.

Squeeze the lime over everything. Serve in warm tortillas with sour cream, avocado and cheese.
de: Chicken, peppers and onions roasted on one pan.

d:
Rub the chicken thighs with the oil and taco seasoning.

Cook in a skillet over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes per side, until cooked through (175°F). Rest 5 minutes, then chop.

Stir the sour cream with the lime zest, lime juice and a pinch of salt to make the crema.

Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave.

Fill the tortillas with chicken, shredded cabbage, cheese and avocado, and drizzle with lime crema.

Corn tortillas and shredded lettuce both work as swaps.
de: Seasoned chicken thighs in tortillas with a cool lime sour cream.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Brown the beef in a skillet and drain. Add the taco seasoning and ⅔ cup water and simmer 5 minutes.

Warm the tortillas so they fold easily. Spread refried beans down the middle of each, then add beef, rice and cheddar. Fold in the sides and roll up.

Place seam-side down in the dish. Warm the queso in the microwave 1 minute and pour it over the burritos.

Bake 15 minutes, until bubbly.
de: Beef and bean burritos smothered in white queso and baked.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Mix the chicken with 1 cup Monterey Jack. Roll about ⅓ cup into each tortilla and place seam-side down in the dish.

Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the broth. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes until thick.

Off the heat, stir in the sour cream and green chiles. Pour the sauce over the enchiladas.

Top with the remaining cheese and bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbly and golden in spots.
de: Chicken enchiladas in a sour cream and green chile white sauce.

d:
Brown the beef in a skillet, drain, and simmer with the taco seasoning and ⅔ cup water 5 minutes. Warm the queso in the microwave 1 minute.

Warm the large tortillas 20 seconds so they fold without cracking. Lay one flat. In the center, layer about ½ cup beef, a drizzle of queso, a tostada shell, then sour cream, lettuce and cheese.

Fold the edges of the large tortilla up and over toward the center, pleating as you go, until it's closed. If a small gap remains in the middle, cover it with a scrap of tortilla.

Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Cook the crunchwraps seam-side down first, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Cut in half to serve.
de: The Taco Bell favorite: beef, queso, a crunchy tostada and cool toppings folded and toasted.

i: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut into chunks
d:
Mix the cumin, oregano and salt and rub it all over the pork.

Put the onion and garlic in the slow cooker, add the pork, and pour over the orange and lime juices.

Cover and cook on low 8 hours (or high 5), until the pork shreds easily.

Heat the broiler. Shred the pork with two forks, spread it on a sheet pan, and spoon ½ cup of the cooking juices over it. Broil 5 minutes, until the edges are crispy.

Warm the tortillas and fill with the pork. Serve with diced onion, cilantro and lime wedges.

Bowl night: serve the crispy pork over rice with pinto beans, Monterey Jack and corn salsa instead of tortillas. Corn tortillas are great here too.
de: Tender orange-lime pork crisped under the broiler.

d:
In a saucepan over medium heat, warm the refried beans and black beans with the cumin, garlic powder and 2 tbsp water, stirring until smooth and hot.

Stir in the cooked rice and season with salt.

Warm the tortillas so they fold without cracking. Spread the bean-rice mixture down the center of each, top with a handful of cheese, fold in the sides and roll up.

Toast the burritos seam-side down in a dry skillet over medium heat 2 minutes per side, until golden. Serve with sour cream (and salsa for the adults).
de: A budget meatless night. They freeze well.

d:
Toss the steak with 2 tbsp oil, the lime juice, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and 1 tsp salt. Let it sit 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the fridge).

Heat the griddle to medium-high. Add the remaining oil, the peppers and onion and cook 6 to 8 minutes, tossing, until soft and charred in spots. Move to the cooler side.

Turn the heat to high. Sear the steak 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium (135°F). Rest 5 minutes.

Warm the tortillas on the griddle 20 seconds per side.

Slice the steak thinly against the grain and serve with the peppers and onions in tortillas, with guacamole and sour cream.

Flank steak works too; slice it extra thin against the grain.
de: Marinated skirt steak seared on the griddle with peppers and onions.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 dish. Start the rice if you don't have it cooked.

Pound thick chicken breasts to an even 1 inch. Rub both sides with the taco seasoning and lay them in the dish.

Stir the queso with the green chiles and pour it over the chicken. Sprinkle with the Monterey Jack.

Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the cheese is bubbly.

Warm the black beans. Serve the chicken and its queso sauce over rice with the beans.
de: Chicken breasts baked under white queso, green chiles and cheese.

i: Optional: 1/4 cup pickled jalapeño slices, for the adults
d:
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a large sheet pan with foil.

Brown the beef in a skillet and drain. Add the taco seasoning and ⅔ cup water and simmer 5 minutes.

Spread half the chips on the pan. Top with half the beef, half the beans and half the cheese. Repeat with the rest.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted.

Warm the queso and drizzle it over. Top with avocado, sour cream and lettuce. Put jalapeños on only the adults' side.
de: Loaded nachos for dinner, built so every chip gets toppings.

d:
Pat the pork dry and season with 2 tsp salt, the cumin and the oregano.

Put the onion and garlic in the slow cooker, add the pork, then pour in the salsa verde, green chiles and broth.

Cover and cook on low 6 to 8 hours (or high 4), until the pork is very tender.

Break the pork into chunks with two forks and stir it into the sauce. Taste for salt.

Serve in warm tortillas (or over rice), with plenty of the green sauce.
de: Slow-cooked pork in tangy salsa verde for tacos, burritos or rice.

d:
Brown the turkey in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, about 7 minutes.

Add the taco seasoning and ⅔ cup water and simmer 5 minutes, until thick.

Separate the lettuce into cups, rinse and pat dry.

Spoon the turkey into the lettuce cups and top with avocado, salsa, cheddar and a dollop of Greek yogurt.
de: Light, crunchy tacos in butter lettuce cups.

i: sour cream and guacamole for dipping
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.

Mix the chicken, softened cream cheese, Monterey Jack, salsa verde, cumin and a pinch of salt until evenly combined.

Warm the tortillas 20 seconds in the microwave so they roll without cracking. Spread about 3 tablespoons of filling along one edge of each and roll up tightly.

Place seam-side down on the pan and spray the tops with cooking spray.

Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until golden and crisp. Serve with sour cream and guacamole for dipping.
de: Rolled crispy tortillas filled with chicken and cream cheese.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Lay the tostada shells on two sheet pans.

Brown the meat in a skillet over medium-high heat and drain. Add the taco seasoning and ⅔ cup water and simmer 5 minutes.

Warm the refried beans with a splash of water so they spread easily. Spread a thin layer on each tostada.

Top with the meat and cheese.

Bake 6 to 8 minutes, until the cheese melts. Top with lettuce, sour cream and avocado.
de: Crispy tostadas spread with beans and topped like a pizza.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Stir the queso, sour cream, green chiles and cumin together. Toss half of this sauce with the chicken, beans and corn.

Lay 2 to 3 tortillas in the dish (tear to fit), then a third of the chicken mixture and a handful of cheese. Repeat two more times.

Top with a final layer of tortillas, spread the remaining sauce over them, and sprinkle with the rest of the cheese.

Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 5 minutes more. Let stand 10 minutes before cutting.
de: Layers of tortillas, chicken, beans and a queso-sour cream sauce.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Lay the bacon on a foil-lined sheet pan and bake 15 to 18 minutes, until crisp.

In a large bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.

In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter. Pour into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; small lumps are fine.

Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and brush with butter. Pour ¼-cup scoops of batter and cook until bubbles cover the surface and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more.

Keep pancakes warm in a 200°F oven while you finish the batch. Serve with syrup and bacon.
de: Fluffy from-scratch pancakes for breakfast-for-dinner night.

i: 1 bag (24 oz) frozen breaded chicken tenders
Optional: 2 tbsp hot honey, for the adults
d:
Bake the chicken tenders per the package. Heat the waffle iron.

In a large bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.

Whisk in the milk, eggs and melted butter just until smooth.

Grease the waffle iron and cook the waffles per its directions, until golden and crisp. Keep warm in a low oven.

Top each waffle with tenders and drizzle with maple syrup (hot honey for the adults).
de: Crispy chicken tenders on Belgian waffles with hot honey or syrup.

i: 1 package (24 oz) fully cooked pork sausage links
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed 13x18-inch sheet pan with parchment and grease it well.

Whisk the pancake mix, milk, eggs and melted butter just until combined; a few lumps are fine.

Pour into the pan and spread evenly. Scatter the blueberries over the batter (and chocolate chips on one section if the kids want them).

Bake 13 to 16 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Warm the sausage links on a second pan in the same oven for the last 8 to 10 minutes.

Cut into squares and serve with syrup and sausage. A spoonful of Greek yogurt on top adds protein and tang.
de: One big pancake, cut into squares. No flipping.
nu:
Calories: 610
Protein: 24g
Carbohydrate: 66g
Fat: 28g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

i: 1 package (12 oz) fully cooked pork sausage links
d:
Whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla and cinnamon in a shallow dish.

Heat a griddle or large skillet over medium heat and melt a little of the butter.

Dip each slice of bread in the egg mixture for about 5 seconds per side, letting the extra drip off.

Cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and set in the middle. Add butter between batches.

Serve with sliced strawberries and maple syrup.

Warm the sausage links in a skillet while the French toast cooks. Thick-sliced Texas toast bread (not the frozen garlic kind) works too.
de: Custardy cinnamon French toast with berries.
nu:
Calories: 620
Protein: 28g
Carbohydrate: 58g
Fat: 30g
Serving Size: 1 of 4 servings

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F.

Melt the butter in a 10-inch oven-safe nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and broccoli (or spinach) 4 minutes, until tender. Add the ham and warm through.

Whisk the eggs with the milk, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Pour over the vegetables and sprinkle with cheddar.

Cook on the stove 2 minutes without stirring, until the edges start to set.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the center is set and no longer jiggles. Rest 5 minutes and cut into wedges.
de: A one-pan egg dinner. Good for leftover veggies.

i: 1 1/2 lb Yukon gold potatoes, diced small
d:
Microwave the diced potatoes in a covered bowl 5 minutes to par-cook them.

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the sausage 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up. Move to a plate.

Add the oil and potatoes to the skillet and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring only every few minutes, until crisp. Add the pepper and onion for the last 4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Stir the sausage back in. Make 4 wells and crack an egg into each.

Cover and cook over medium-low 4 to 5 minutes, until the whites are set. Sprinkle with cheddar and serve from the pan.
de: Crispy potatoes, sausage and peppers topped with fried eggs.

d:
Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper and scramble them in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat until softly set. Move to a bowl.

Lay out the tortillas. On half of each, layer cheese, eggs, bacon and a little more cheese, then fold over.

Melt a little butter in the skillet over medium heat. Cook the quesadillas 2 minutes per side, until golden and melted.

Cut into wedges and serve with salsa verde or sour cream.
de: Scrambled eggs, bacon and cheese in crispy tortillas.

d:
Put the chicken in the slow cooker. Set the block of cream cheese on top, sprinkle with the ranch seasoning, and pour in the broth.

Cover and cook on low 4 to 6 hours (or high 2 to 3), until the chicken shreds easily (165°F).

Shred the chicken with two forks right in the pot and stir until the cream cheese coats everything.

Stir in the bacon and cheddar until the cheese melts.

Toast the buns and pile on the chicken.
de: Creamy ranch-bacon chicken for sandwiches, wraps or over rice.

d:
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic and basil. Put the chicken in the slow cooker and pour the sauce over it.

Cover and cook on low 4 hours (or high 2), until the chicken is tender.

Move the chicken to a plate. Stir the cornstarch with 2 tbsp water, whisk it into the sauce, and cook on high, uncovered, 10 minutes until thickened.

Meanwhile, cook the rice and steam the broccoli.

Shred or slice the chicken and toss it in the thickened sauce. Serve over rice with broccoli.
de: Sticky honey-garlic chicken thighs over rice.

i: 2 cans (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Put the chicken, cream of chicken soup, broth, onion, carrots, celery and thyme in the slow cooker and stir.

Cover and cook on low 6 hours (or high 3 to 4).

Lift out the chicken, shred it, and stir it back in.

Turn the cooker to high. Tear each biscuit into 4 pieces and drop them over the top in a single layer.

Cover and cook 45 to 60 minutes, until the dumplings are fluffy and cooked through in the center (break one open to check). Season with salt and pepper.
de: Creamy chicken stew with biscuit dumplings.

d:
In a bowl, gently mix the beef, breadcrumbs, egg and half the onion soup mix. Shape into 6 oval patties about ¾ inch thick.

Brown the patties in a hot skillet 2 minutes per side (they finish in the slow cooker).

Whisk the gravy mixes, the rest of the onion soup mix and the water until smooth.

Layer the patties and mushrooms in the slow cooker and pour the gravy over them.

Cover and cook on low 6 hours (or high 3). Serve the patties and gravy over mashed potatoes.
de: Frozen-patty or homemade Salisbury steak in onion gravy. Serve over mashed potatoes.

n: Slow Cooker Salsa Verde Chicken Tacos
i: shredded cheese, sour cream and avocado for topping
d:
Put the chicken in the slow cooker. Sprinkle with the taco seasoning and pour the salsa verde over it.

Cover and cook on low 4 to 6 hours (or high 2 to 3), until the chicken shreds easily.

Shred the chicken with two forks and stir it into the juices so it soaks them up.

Warm the tortillas and fill with chicken, using a slotted spoon. Top with cheese, sour cream and avocado.
de: Three ingredients, shredded and ready for tacos, nachos or bowls.

d:
Add the macaroni, water, butter, salt and dry mustard to the Instant Pot and stir so the pasta is under the water.

Lock the lid and cook on high pressure 4 minutes. Do a quick release (cover the vent with a towel; it can sputter).

Stir well. With the pot on Keep Warm, stir in the milk, then the cheddar and mozzarella a handful at a time until creamy.

Season with salt and pepper. It thickens as it sits; stir in a splash of milk if needed.
de: Creamy mac and cheese in about 15 minutes.

i: 2 cups long grain white rice, rinsed
d:
Season the chicken with the paprika, garlic powder and 1 tsp salt. Turn the Instant Pot to Sauté, add the oil, and sear the chicken 2 minutes per side. Move to a plate.

Add the onion and cook 3 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds. Pour in a splash of the broth and scrape the bottom clean (this prevents a burn warning).

Stir in the rinsed rice and the rest of the broth. Lay the chicken on top.

Lock the lid and cook on high pressure 10 minutes. Let it release naturally for 10 minutes, then release the rest.

Stir in the frozen peas (the heat cooks them) and fluff the rice. Check the chicken reaches 175°F.
de: Seasoned chicken and fluffy rice done together.

n: Slow Cooker Pork Chops and Gravy
i: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
d:
Season the pork chops with pepper and lay them in the slow cooker.

Whisk the cream of chicken soup, gravy mix, ranch seasoning and broth until smooth and pour it over the chops.

Cover and cook on low 3½ to 4 hours (no longer; lean chops dry out), until the chops are tender and at least 145°F.

Stir the gravy and serve the chops with mashed potatoes and plenty of gravy.
de: Fork-tender pork chops in creamy gravy over mashed potatoes.

d:
Put the chicken in the slow cooker. Add the broth, Italian seasoning, garlic and sun-dried tomatoes.

Cover and cook on low 4 hours (or high 2), until the chicken reaches 165°F.

Stir in the cream and parmesan. Add the spinach, cover, and cook 15 minutes more, until wilted and the sauce is creamy.

Slice or shred the chicken and serve over the cooked penne (or rice) with the sauce.
de: Chicken in a garlic parmesan cream sauce with sun-dried tomatoes and spinach.

i: 1 bag (12 oz) frozen cut green beans
d:
Put the potatoes, onion and broth in the bottom of the slow cooker and lay the kielbasa on top.

Stir the melted butter with the garlic powder, Italian seasoning and ½ tsp salt and drizzle it over everything.

Cover and cook on low 5 to 6 hours (or high 3), until the potatoes are tender when poked.

Stir in the frozen green beans, turn to high, cover, and cook 30 minutes more, until the beans are hot and crisp-tender. Taste for salt and serve with mustard on the side.
de: Smoked sausage, baby potatoes and green beans in garlic butter.

i: 1 1/2 lb flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
d:
Turn the Instant Pot to Sauté and add the oil. Brown the beef in two batches, 2 minutes each.

Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the broth, soy sauce, brown sugar and sesame oil, scraping the bottom clean.

Lock the lid and cook on high pressure 10 minutes. Quick release. Meanwhile, cook the rice and steam the broccoli.

Turn back to Sauté. Stir the cornstarch with 3 tbsp water and stir it in. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce thickens.

Toss in the broccoli and serve over rice.

Thinly sliced chuck works too and gets even more tender under pressure.
de: Tender beef in a savory sauce with bright broccoli.

d:
Put the chicken in the slow cooker.

Whisk the BBQ sauce, brown sugar, cider vinegar and smoked paprika and pour it over the chicken.

Cover and cook on low 4 to 6 hours (or high 2 to 3), until the chicken shreds easily.

Shred the chicken in the pot and stir it into the sauce.

Toast the buns and pile on the chicken. Top with coleslaw.
de: Sweet and smoky shredded chicken for sliders.

n: Blackstone Hibachi Chicken and Fried Rice
d:
Make the yum yum sauce: stir the mayonnaise, ketchup, sugar, garlic powder and 1 tbsp water. Chill until serving.

Heat the griddle to medium-high. Cook the zucchini, onion and mushrooms with 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp soy sauce 6 to 8 minutes, until tender. Move to the cool side.

Cook the chicken with 1 tbsp butter, the garlic and 1 tbsp soy sauce 6 to 8 minutes, until cooked through (165°F).

Scramble the eggs on the griddle, then add the cold rice, the remaining butter and soy sauce, and fry 4 minutes, chopping and tossing until hot and slightly crisp.

Serve the chicken, vegetables and fried rice with yum yum sauce.
de: Hibachi night at home with yum yum sauce.

d:
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, Italian seasoning, paprika and 1 tsp salt. Toss with the chicken and marinate at least 15 minutes (up to 4 hours in the fridge). If using wooden skewers, soak them now.

Thread the chicken, peppers, onion and zucchini onto skewers, alternating.

Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates.

Grill 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are charred.

Serve with warm pita (or rice) and a squeeze of lemon.
de: Marinated chicken and veggie skewers on the grill.

d:
Pat the chops dry and season with the paprika, garlic powder, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper.

Make the glaze: simmer the honey, soy sauce, garlic and butter in a small pan 2 minutes.

Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates.

Grill the chops 4 to 5 minutes per side, brushing with the glaze during the last 2 minutes, until they reach 145°F.

Rest 5 minutes and drizzle with the rest of the glaze.
de: Juicy chops with a sticky honey garlic glaze.

d:
Toss the drumsticks with the oil, brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and 1½ tsp salt.

Set up the grill for two-zone heat (burners on one side only, medium) and cook the drumsticks on the cool side with the lid closed for 30 to 35 minutes, turning occasionally.

Move them to the hot side and brush with BBQ sauce.

Grill 5 minutes more, turning and brushing, until caramelized and the meat reaches 175°F near the bone.
de: Kid-friendly drumsticks with a sweet BBQ glaze.

d:
Toss the steak tips with the oil, Worcestershire, garlic powder, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper. Let sit while the grill heats.

Heat the grill to high and oil the grates.

Grill the tips 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium (135°F). Rest 5 minutes.

Stir the melted butter with the garlic and parsley and toss the steak in it.
de: Sirloin tips grilled on skewers and tossed in garlic herb butter.

d:
Toss the chicken with half the teriyaki and marinate 15 minutes. Soak wooden skewers in water if using.

Start the rice.

Thread the chicken, pineapple, bell pepper and onion onto skewers.

Grill over medium-high heat 10 to 12 minutes, turning and brushing with the remaining teriyaki in the last few minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.

Serve over rice.
de: Teriyaki chicken, pineapple and peppers on the grill.

d:
Pound the chicken to an even ¾ inch so it cooks evenly.

Toss it with the oil, lemon zest, half the lemon juice, lemon pepper seasoning and garlic powder. Let sit 10 minutes while the grill heats.

Grill over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes per side, until it reaches 165°F.

Stir the melted butter with the remaining lemon juice and brush it over the chicken before serving.
de: Simple, bright grilled chicken that goes with any side.

n: Grilled Pork Tenderloin with Dry Rub
d:
Mix the brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme and salt.

Pat the tenderloins dry, rub with the oil, then coat with the spice mix.

Heat the grill to medium-high. Grill the pork, turning every 4 to 5 minutes, 18 to 22 minutes total, until it reaches 145°F in the thickest part.

Rest 5 minutes before slicing into medallions.
de: A sweet-smoky rub on a quick-grilling cut.

d:
Mix the sauce: soy sauce, Worcestershire, ketchup and brown sugar. Cook the ramen noodles 2 minutes and drain (discard the flavor packets).

Heat the griddle to medium-high. Cook the chicken in 1 tbsp oil 5 to 6 minutes, until cooked through.

Add the remaining oil, cabbage, carrots and onion and cook 4 minutes, tossing, until crisp-tender.

Add the noodles and the sauce and toss with two spatulas for 2 to 3 minutes until everything is coated and hot.
de: Griddle noodles with chicken, cabbage and a sweet-savory sauce.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with foil.

Toss the halved potatoes with 2 tbsp oil, the garlic powder, Italian seasoning, paprika and ½ tsp salt. Spread cut-side down on the pan and roast 15 minutes.

Toss the sausage and green beans with the remaining oil and a pinch of salt. Add them to the pan and stir everything together.

Roast 15 to 20 minutes more, until the potatoes are golden and tender and the sausage is browned.

Sprinkle with parmesan and serve straight from the pan.
de: Smoked sausage, potatoes and green beans roasted on one pan.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a rimmed sheet pan with foil. Pat the chicken very dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.

Set the thighs skin-side up on the pan with space between them. Roast 25 minutes, until the skin is golden and starting to crisp.

Meanwhile, whisk the honey, Dijon, yellow mustard, garlic and thyme in a small saucepan and simmer 2 minutes.

Brush half the glaze over the thighs and roast 8 to 10 minutes more, until glossy and the meat reaches 175°F.

Rest 5 minutes and spoon the rest of the glaze over each thigh. Taste the glaze before serving; a pinch of salt or squeeze of lemon balances the honey.
de: Crispy-skinned thighs with a sweet honey mustard glaze.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Pat the chops dry and season lightly with salt and pepper.

Mix the panko, parmesan, garlic powder and Italian seasoning in a shallow dish. Beat the eggs in another dish.

Dip each chop in egg, let the extra drip off, then press firmly into the crumbs on both sides.

Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chops 3 minutes per side, until golden.

Move the skillet to the oven and bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the chops reach 145°F. Rest 5 minutes.
de: Crispy panko-parmesan crust and juicy chops.

n: Homemade Chicken Tenders with Honey Mustard
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Set a wire rack on a sheet pan and spray it with oil.

Mix the panko, Italian breadcrumbs, parmesan, garlic powder, paprika and ½ tsp salt in a shallow dish. Beat the eggs in another dish.

Dip each tender in egg, then press into the crumbs to coat well. Lay on the rack without touching.

Spray the tops with cooking spray. Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until golden and cooked through (165°F). No need to flip with the rack.

Whisk the honey, Dijon and mayonnaise for the dipping sauce and serve alongside.
de: Crispy oven-fried tenders that beat the frozen ones.

d:
Mix the beef, panko, egg, Worcestershire, onion powder, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper with your hands until just combined. Shape into 4 oval patties about ¾ inch thick.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the patties 4 minutes per side. Move to a plate (they'll finish in the gravy).

Lower the heat to medium. Melt the butter in the skillet and cook the mushrooms and onion 6 minutes, until browned.

Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the broth. Simmer 3 minutes, until it thickens.

Return the patties to the gravy, cover, and simmer 10 minutes, until cooked through (160°F). Serve with mashed potatoes or egg noodles.
de: Diner classic. Serve with mashed potatoes and green beans.

n: Garlic Butter Chicken Bites and Potatoes
d:
Microwave the quartered potatoes in a covered bowl 5 minutes to par-cook.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the potatoes 8 to 10 minutes, turning occasionally, until crisp. Season with salt and move to a plate.

Season the chicken with salt, pepper and the paprika. Add it to the skillet and cook 6 to 7 minutes, until browned and cooked through.

Lower the heat to medium. Return the potatoes and add the butter, garlic and Italian seasoning. Toss 1 minute until fragrant and coated.

Top with parmesan and serve.
de: Skillet chicken and crispy baby potatoes in garlic butter.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and line a sheet pan with foil.

In a large bowl, soak the panko in the milk for 5 minutes, until soft.

Add the beef, eggs, grated onion, Worcestershire, garlic powder and salt. Mix gently with your hands just until combined (overmixing makes it dense).

Shape into a 9x5-inch loaf on the pan. Bake 40 minutes.

Stir the BBQ sauce with the brown sugar and brush it over the loaf. Bake 15 minutes more, until it reaches 160°F. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
de: Tender meatloaf with a BBQ glaze instead of the usual ketchup.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with foil.

Toss the sweet potato with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt and roast 10 minutes (it takes longer than everything else).

Toss the chicken, broccoli and bell pepper with the remaining oil, the garlic powder, Italian seasoning, paprika and ¾ tsp salt.

Add them to the pan with the sweet potato and spread out in a single layer.

Roast 15 to 18 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are browned at the edges.
de: Chicken, broccoli, peppers and sweet potatoes on one pan.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a large sheet pan with foil.

Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and half the ranch seasoning. Roast 15 minutes.

Push the potatoes to the sides. Lay the chops in the middle and arrange the green beans around them.

Stir the remaining oil, the melted butter and the rest of the ranch, and brush it over the chops and beans.

Roast 18 to 20 minutes, until the pork reaches 145°F. Rest the chops 5 minutes before serving.
de: A three-ingredient seasoning on a whole sheet pan dinner.

d:
Season the flour with the garlic powder, paprika, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper in a shallow dish. Whisk the eggs with ½ cup milk in another dish.

Pat the steaks dry. Dredge each in flour, dip in egg, then dredge in flour again, pressing so it sticks.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Fry 2 steaks at a time, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden. Drain on a rack or paper towels.

Pour off all but 3 tbsp oil, leaving the browned bits. Whisk in 3 tbsp of the leftover seasoned flour and cook 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the 2 cups whole milk and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until thick. Season with plenty of black pepper and salt. Spoon over the steaks.
de: Crispy cube steaks with peppery cream gravy.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Set a wire rack on a foil-lined sheet pan.

Pat the drumsticks very dry with paper towels; this is the key to crisp skin.

Toss them with the oil, then the baking powder (not baking soda), garlic powder, paprika, onion powder and salt.

Arrange on the rack without touching. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, flipping halfway, until the skin is crisp and the meat reaches 175°F near the bone.
de: Seasoned drumsticks, crispy and kid-friendly with almost no work.

i: 1 box (16 oz) frozen potato and cheese pierogies
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with foil.

On the pan, toss the frozen pierogies, kielbasa, bell pepper and onion with the oil, garlic powder and ½ tsp salt. Spread in a single layer.

Roast 20 to 25 minutes, flipping everything halfway, until the pierogies are golden and crisp on both sides.

Serve with sour cream for dipping.
de: Frozen pierogies, sausage and peppers roasted on one pan.

d:
Season the flour with ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Dredge the chicken, shaking off the extra; save the leftover flour.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken 4 minutes per side. Move to a plate.

Lower the heat to medium. Melt the butter and cook the onion 8 minutes, until soft and golden. Add the garlic and 1 tbsp of the leftover flour and stir 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the broth, then the cream and thyme. Bring to a simmer.

Return the chicken, cover, and simmer 8 minutes, until it reaches 165°F and the gravy has thickened. Serve over mashed potatoes or rice.
de: Pan-seared chicken in a rich onion gravy over rice or mashed potatoes.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Scrub the potatoes, dry them, and prick each several times with a fork.

Rub with the oil and sprinkle with salt. Bake directly on the oven rack 50 to 60 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. (Short on time: microwave 8 to 10 minutes, then bake 15 minutes to crisp the skin.)

While they bake, warm the chicken (leftover chili works too) and steam the broccoli.

Split each potato, fluff the inside with a fork, and add a pat of butter.

Set out the toppings and let everyone build their own.
de: Set out toppings and everyone builds their own. Good for leftover chili or chicken.
nu:
Calories: 560
Protein: 32g
Carbohydrate: 58g
Fat: 22g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

n: Lemon Garlic Chicken and Asparagus Skillet
d:
Season the chicken with salt, pepper and the Italian seasoning.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Move to a plate.

Melt the butter in the skillet. Add the asparagus and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Return the chicken, squeeze in the lemon juice, and toss. Sprinkle with parmesan and serve.
de: A light one-skillet dinner ready in 25 minutes.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Scrub the sweet potatoes, prick them with a fork, and bake on a foil-lined pan 40 to 45 minutes, until very soft. (Or microwave 10 to 12 minutes, turning halfway.)

Warm the chicken with the BBQ sauce in a skillet, 3 to 4 minutes.

Split each sweet potato and fluff the inside with a fork. Season with a pinch of salt.

Fill with BBQ chicken and top with cheddar, a spoonful of Greek yogurt and green onions.
de: Roasted sweet potatoes topped with BBQ chicken and a little cheese.

d:
In a bowl, gently mix the turkey, feta, chopped spinach, oregano, garlic powder and ½ tsp salt. Shape into 4 patties about ¾ inch thick and press a dimple in the center of each.

Heat a grill or skillet to medium-high and oil it.

Cook the patties 5 to 6 minutes per side, until they reach 165°F.

Toast the buns. Serve the burgers with tzatziki and cucumber slices.
de: Juicy turkey burgers with feta and spinach, served with tzatziki.

n: Chicken Sausage and Veggie Sheet Pan
i: 2 packages (12 oz) fully cooked chicken sausage, sliced
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil.

Toss the sweet potato, Brussels sprouts and red onion with the oil, garlic powder and ½ tsp salt. Spread out, with the sprouts cut-side down, and roast 15 minutes.

Add the sausage slices to the pan and drizzle everything with the maple syrup. Toss.

Roast 10 to 12 minutes more, until the sprouts are browned and the sausage is hot and caramelized.
de: Chicken sausage, sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts with a maple glaze.
nu:
Calories: 480
Protein: 30g
Carbohydrate: 34g
Fat: 24g
Serving Size: 1 of 4 servings

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Pound thick chicken breasts to an even ¾ to 1 inch.

Lay the chicken in a baking dish and season with salt and pepper.

Spread 2 tablespoons pesto over each breast, then top with the tomatoes and mozzarella.

Bake 22 to 25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the cheese is bubbly. Broil 1 minute to brown the top if you like.
de: Chicken breasts topped with pesto, tomatoes and mozzarella.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and set the flatbreads on a sheet pan.

Spread each flatbread with Alfredo sauce, leaving a small border.

Top with chicken, spinach, mozzarella and parmesan.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the edges are crisp. Slice into strips.
de: Naan or flatbread topped with Alfredo, chicken, spinach and mozzarella.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Set the bread halves cut-side up on a sheet pan.

Mix the softened butter with the garlic and spread it over the cut sides.

Dollop the ricotta over the bread, then cover with mozzarella and parmesan. Add the pepperoni and sprinkle with Italian seasoning.

Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the edges are golden. Cut into slices.
de: French bread with garlic butter, mozzarella and pepperoni. No red sauce.

d:
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack in the lowest position. Let the dough sit at room temperature 20 minutes so it stretches easily.

Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan (or use the prebaked crust).

Spread with BBQ sauce, then top with the chicken, red onion, mozzarella and smoked gouda.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes (8 to 10 for a prebaked crust), until the crust is golden underneath and the cheese bubbles.

Sprinkle with cilantro, let cool 2 minutes, and slice.
de: BBQ sauce base, chicken, red onion, mozzarella and gouda.

d:
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack in the lowest position. Let the dough rest at room temperature 20 minutes.

Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan (or use the prebaked crust).

Spread the ranch over the dough, then top with chicken, bacon, mozzarella and cheddar.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes (8 to 10 for a prebaked crust), until golden and bubbly.

Top with green onions and slice.
de: Ranch base with chicken, bacon and cheddar-mozzarella.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and set the naan on a sheet pan.

Stir the olive oil with the garlic and brush it over the naan.

Top with mozzarella, parmesan and everyone's choice of toppings.

Bake 8 minutes, until the cheese melts and the edges crisp.
de: Fast personal pizzas the kids can top themselves.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Let the dough rest at room temperature 20 minutes.

Mix the ricotta, mozzarella, parmesan, ham (or pepperoni) and Italian seasoning.

Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll each into an 8-inch circle on a floured counter.

Spoon a quarter of the filling onto half of each circle, leaving a 1-inch border. Fold over and crimp the edges firmly with a fork.

Brush with the beaten egg and cut a small slit in each top. Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until deep golden. Rest 5 minutes; the filling is very hot.
de: Pizza dough folded around ricotta, mozzarella and ham or pepperoni.

i: 2 cans (8 oz) refrigerated crescent dough sheets
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9-inch round or square pan.

Unroll the dough sheets and press any seams together. Cover each with pepperoni and mozzarella.

Roll up from a long side and slice into 1-inch rolls. Set them cut-side up in the pan, snug together.

Stir the melted butter with the garlic powder and Italian seasoning, brush it over the rolls, and sprinkle with parmesan.

Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until golden and cooked through in the center. Serve warm.
de: Crescent dough rolled with pepperoni and mozzarella, with garlic butter for dipping.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F.

Mix the softened butter with the garlic, parsley and a pinch of salt.

Spread over the cut sides of the bread and top with mozzarella and parmesan.

Bake on a sheet pan 10 minutes, then broil 1 minute until golden, watching closely. Slice and serve.
de: Ready in 15 minutes and goes with every pasta night.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F.

Toss the broccoli with the oil, garlic powder and ½ tsp salt. Spread on a sheet pan with space between the florets.

Roast 15 minutes, until browned at the edges.

Sprinkle with parmesan and roast 3 minutes more. Squeeze the lemon over the top before serving.
de: Crispy-edged broccoli that kids eat.

d:
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Add the frozen corn and cook 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until hot and lightly browned.

Lower the heat and stir in the honey and cream cheese until melted and creamy.

Season with salt and pepper and serve.
de: Sweet, buttery corn in 10 minutes.

d:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the green beans 4 minutes, until bright green, then drain.

In a large skillet over medium heat, cook the bacon until crisp, about 6 minutes.

Add the garlic and butter and cook 30 seconds.

Toss in the green beans and cook 2 minutes, until coated and hot. Season with salt and pepper.
de: Garlicky green beans tossed with crispy bacon.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F with a sheet pan inside to preheat.

Toss the potatoes with the oil, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, paprika and 1 tsp salt.

Carefully spread them on the hot pan in a single layer (they should sizzle).

Roast 35 minutes, flipping once halfway, until golden and crisp outside and tender inside.
de: Golden roasted potatoes with garlic and herbs.

d:
Rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear.

Bring the water, butter and 1 tsp salt to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in the rice, cover, and lower the heat to low.

Cook 18 minutes without lifting the lid, then turn off the heat and let it stand covered 5 minutes.

Fluff with a fork and stir in the lime zest, lime juice and cilantro.
de: Chipotle-style rice for taco nights and bowls.

d:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and melt the butter.

Add the corn in an even layer and let it sit 2 minutes to char before stirring. Cook 6 to 8 minutes total, until browned in spots.

Off the heat, stir in the mayonnaise, sour cream, lime juice and half the cotija.

Spoon into cups and top with the remaining cotija and a light sprinkle of chili powder (skip it on the kids' cups if they like).
de: Elote-style corn with mayo, lime, cotija and chili powder.

d:
Slice the cucumbers and onion as thinly as you can.

In a bowl, whisk the sour cream, vinegar, sugar, dill and ½ tsp salt.

Add the cucumbers and onion and toss to coat.

Chill at least 15 minutes. Stir before serving.
de: A cool, crunchy side for grilled meats.

d:
Simmer the baby carrots in salted water 8 minutes, until just tender. Drain.

Melt the butter with the honey in the same pan over medium heat.

Add the carrots and thyme and toss 3 minutes, until glazed and shiny. Season with a pinch of salt.
de: Tender carrots in a buttery honey glaze.

d:
Wash and prepare the fruit: quarter the strawberries, halve the grapes and slice the kiwis.

Combine all the fruit in a large bowl.

Whisk the honey and lime juice, pour it over the fruit, and toss gently.

Chill until serving; it's best within a day.
de: A bright side for breakfast-for-dinner or sandwich night.

d:
Wash and dry the romaine well (wet lettuce makes the dressing slide off).

Whisk the mayonnaise, grated parmesan, lemon juice, Dijon, garlic and a good pinch of pepper with 1 tbsp water. Bottled Caesar usually contains anchovies; this keeps it seafood-free.

Toss the romaine with the dressing until every leaf is coated.

Top with croutons and shaved parmesan and serve right away.
de: A crunchy side salad with store-bought shortcuts.

i: 3 lb Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cubed
d:
Put the potatoes and garlic cloves in a pot, cover with cold water, and add 1 tbsp salt.

Bring to a boil and simmer 15 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.

Drain well and return to the pot over low heat for 1 minute to dry them out.

Mash with the butter, then the warm milk and sour cream until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
de: Creamy mashed potatoes for Salisbury steak, smothered chicken and roasts.

n: Sheet Pan Hawaiian Pizza (Garlic Butter Base)
i: 1 can (20 oz) pineapple chunks, drained and patted dry
d:
Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the lowest position. Let the dough sit at room temperature 20 minutes so it stretches easily.

Oil a rimmed sheet pan and press the dough into the corners. If it springs back, rest it 5 minutes and try again.

Stir the melted butter with the garlic and Italian seasoning and brush it all over the dough, right to the edges.

Cover with mozzarella, then scatter the ham and pineapple. Sprinkle with parmesan.

Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until the crust is golden underneath and the cheese is browned in spots. Cool 3 minutes, then cut into squares.
de: Ham and pineapple on a garlic butter crust, no red sauce needed.

d:
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack low. Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan (or use the prebaked crust).

Spread the ranch over the dough.

Toss half the chicken with the buffalo sauce. Put the plain chicken on the kids' half and the buffalo chicken on the other.

Top with the mozzarella and cheddar.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes (8 to 10 for a prebaked crust), until golden and bubbly. Sprinkle with green onions and drizzle a little extra ranch before slicing.
de: Ranch instead of red sauce, with buffalo chicken on the grown-ups' half.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Let the dough rest at room temperature 20 minutes.

Roll the dough on a floured counter into a 10x14-inch rectangle.

Layer the provolone, ham and pepperoni over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border, then sprinkle with mozzarella and Italian seasoning.

Roll up from a long side, pinch the seam and ends shut, and set seam-side down on the pan. Brush with the egg and cut 4 small slits on top.

Bake 22 to 25 minutes, until deep golden. Rest 10 minutes, then slice. Serve with the melted butter stirred with the garlic for dipping.
de: A rolled, sliced pizza loaf with garlic butter for dipping instead of marinara.

i: 2 cans (8 oz) refrigerated crescent dough sheets
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.

Unroll each dough sheet and cut it into 4 rectangles (8 total). Press any seams closed.

On half of each rectangle, spread a spoonful of ricotta, sprinkle with Italian seasoning, and add 3 pepperoni and a handful of mozzarella.

Fold the dough over and press the edges with a fork to seal. Set on the pan and brush with butter, then sprinkle with parmesan.

Bake 12 to 14 minutes, until golden. Cool 5 minutes; the filling is hot.
de: Crescent dough pockets filled with cheese and pepperoni; kids can make their own.

d:
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack low. Let the dough rest at room temperature 20 minutes.

Brown the sausage in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook 5 minutes more until browned. Drain any fat.

Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan. Stir the garlic into the Alfredo and spread it over the dough.

Top with mozzarella, the sausage and mushrooms, and the parmesan.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the crust is golden underneath. Rest 2 minutes and slice.
de: Garlic cream sauce, Italian sausage and mushrooms on a crisp crust.

d:
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack low. Let the dough rest 20 minutes.

Cook the pepper and onion in the oil over medium-high heat 5 minutes. Add the steak, season with salt and pepper, and cook 2 to 3 minutes until just browned. Drain.

Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan. Brush with the butter mixed with garlic.

Lay the provolone over the dough, add the steak mixture, and top with mozzarella.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until golden and bubbly. Slice and serve.
de: Shaved steak, peppers and onions on a provolone garlic-butter pizza.

d:
Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack low.

Brown the beef and drain. Add the taco seasoning and ⅔ cup water and simmer 5 minutes until thick.

Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan. Warm the refried beans with 2 tbsp water and spread them over the dough.

Top with the beef and cheese. Bake 14 to 16 minutes (8 to 10 for a prebaked crust), until the crust is golden.

Top with lettuce, dollops of sour cream and crushed chips. Add salsa to the adults' slices.
de: Refried bean base, taco beef and cheese, finished with cool toppings.

i: 1 box (10 oz) frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
1 can (14 oz) artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
d:
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack low. Let the dough rest 20 minutes.

Stir the cream cheese, sour cream, garlic and half the parmesan until smooth. Fold in the spinach and artichokes and season with salt and pepper.

Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan and spread the spinach mixture over it.

Top with mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until golden underneath and bubbly on top.
de: Like the dip, on a pizza. Meatless and creamy.

d:
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack low. Let the dough rest 20 minutes.

Brown the beef with ½ tsp salt and drain.

Stir the mayonnaise, ketchup and mustard into a burger sauce. Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan and spread half the sauce on it.

Top with mozzarella, beef, bacon and cheddar. Bake 12 to 15 minutes until golden.

Top with lettuce and pickles and drizzle with the rest of the sauce.
de: Burger sauce, beef, bacon and cheddar, topped with pickles if you like.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and set the naan on a sheet pan.

Spread the pesto over each naan.

Top with chicken, mozzarella slices, tomatoes and parmesan.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese melts. Slice into strips.
de: Naan flatbreads with pesto, chicken and fresh mozzarella in 15 minutes.

d:
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack low. Let the dough rest 20 minutes.

Stretch the dough on an oiled sheet pan.

Spread the sauce thinly, leaving a 1-inch border. For a white pizza, brush with garlic butter or Alfredo instead.

Top with mozzarella, pepperoni, oregano and parmesan.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the crust is golden underneath and the pepperoni curls. Rest 2 minutes before slicing.
de: A from-scratch-crust pepperoni pizza; use the white-sauce swap for the kids.

i: 2 cans (8 oz) refrigerated crescent dough sheets
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Press the dough into a greased sheet pan, sealing the seams, and bake 8 minutes until lightly golden.

Brown the sausage in a skillet. Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute, then slowly add the milk and simmer until thick. Season with pepper.

Scramble the eggs in a separate pan until just set and season with salt.

Spread the gravy over the crust, top with the eggs and cheddar.

Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until the cheese melts. Sprinkle with green onions and cut into squares.
de: Breakfast for dinner: sausage gravy, scrambled eggs and cheddar on a crescent crust.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line two sheet pans with foil.

Stir the butter with the garlic. Brush each pita with garlic butter or spread with Alfredo.

Set out the cheese and toppings and let everyone build their own.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese melts and the edges crisp.
de: Everyone builds their own on pita with a garlic butter or Alfredo base.

i: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
d:
Start the rice and steam the broccoli.

Beat the egg in a bowl, add the chicken and toss, then toss with all but 1 tbsp of the cornstarch until coated.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken in batches 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until crisp and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.

Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, brown sugar, rice vinegar, broth and the remaining 1 tbsp cornstarch. Pour off all but 1 tsp oil, add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the sauce and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until glossy.

Toss the chicken in the sauce and serve over rice with broccoli and green onions. Red pepper flakes go on the adults' plates.
de: Crispy chicken in the takeout-style sweet, tangy sauce, without the heat.

i: 1 1/2 lb chicken breast, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
d:
Start the rice. Toss the chicken with the cornstarch and a pinch of salt.

Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, honey, vinegar, sesame oil and 3 tbsp water.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the chicken 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through.

Add the pepper, zucchini and garlic and cook 2 minutes. Pour in the sauce and simmer 1 minute until glossy.

Stir in the peanuts and green onions and serve over rice. Pass red pepper flakes or chili oil for the adults.
de: Peanuts, peppers and a savory-sweet sauce; the chiles stay on the side.

d:
Start the rice. Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and honey for the sauce.

Season the cutlets with salt and pepper. Dredge in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the panko.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat until a crumb sizzles. Fry the cutlets 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through (165°F).

Drain on a rack for 2 minutes, then slice into strips.

Serve over rice with shredded cabbage and the tonkatsu sauce drizzled over or on the side.
de: Crispy panko chicken cutlets with the sweet-savory Japanese dipping sauce.

d:
Soak the rice noodles in very hot tap water 8 to 10 minutes, until bendable but still firm. Drain.

Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, rice vinegar and ketchup.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the chicken 4 to 5 minutes until cooked. Push aside, add the eggs and scramble until set.

Add the remaining oil, garlic, noodles and sauce. Toss with tongs 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles absorb the sauce and soften.

Toss in the carrots (or bean sprouts) and green onions. Serve with peanuts and lime wedges.
de: Rice noodles, chicken and egg in a sweet-tangy peanut-free sauce.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment.

Toss the frozen potstickers and vegetables with the oil and spread out in a single layer.

Roast 18 to 20 minutes, flipping halfway, until the potstickers are crisp and golden at the edges.

Whisk the soy sauce, honey, sesame oil and garlic. Drizzle over the pan and toss.

Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve, with rice if you want more.
de: Frozen potstickers and vegetables roasted together with a sweet soy glaze.

i: 1 1/2 lb chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
d:
Start the rice and steam the broccoli.

Candy the walnuts: cook them with 2 tbsp honey in a dry skillet over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until glossy. Spread on parchment to cool.

Toss the chicken with the beaten egg, then the cornstarch and a pinch of salt. Fry in the oil in batches 5 to 6 minutes until golden and cooked through.

Whisk the mayonnaise, condensed milk (or honey), lemon juice and the remaining honey.

Toss the hot chicken in the sauce and top with the candied walnuts. Serve over rice with broccoli.
de: Like the takeout honey walnut shrimp, made with crispy chicken.

d:
Start the rice.

Brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat 6 to 7 minutes, breaking it up. Drain the fat.

Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.

Stir in the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil and grated pear (it adds sweetness, like a marinade). Simmer 3 minutes until glossy.

Serve over rice with cucumber, carrots, green onions and sesame seeds. Gochujang mayo is great for the adults.
de: Sweet soy-garlic ground beef over rice; mild and quick.

d:
Start the rice. Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp cornstarch and a pinch of salt.

Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, brown sugar, broth and the remaining cornstarch.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add the broccoli and 2 tbsp water, cover, and steam 2 minutes. Move to a plate.

Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the chicken 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.

Pour in the sauce, return the broccoli, and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until glossy. Serve over rice.
de: Tender chicken and broccoli in a classic brown garlic sauce.

i: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cubed
d:
Toss the chicken with the yogurt, 1 tsp garam masala, the cumin, turmeric and 1 tsp salt. Let sit while you start the rice (or up to overnight in the fridge).

Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 6 to 7 minutes until browned in spots. Move to a plate.

Melt the remaining butter and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger and remaining garam masala for 1 minute, then the tomato paste for 1 minute.

Stir in the cream, broth and honey and simmer 5 minutes until thickened. Return the chicken and simmer 5 minutes more until cooked through.

Season with salt and serve over rice with warm naan.
de: Creamy, gently spiced Indian butter chicken; just a little tomato for color.

d:
Start the rice.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 6 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and garam masala and stir 1 minute.

Add the chicken and 1 tsp salt and cook 4 minutes, stirring.

Pour in the coconut milk and honey and simmer 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens.

Turn off the heat and stir in the yogurt. Top with almonds and cilantro and serve over rice.
de: A mild, creamy coconut-and-yogurt curry with no tomato at all.

d:
Start the rice.

Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.

Add the potatoes, chickpeas, coconut milk, broth and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.

Mash a few potatoes against the pot to thicken the sauce. Stir in the spinach until wilted.

Squeeze in half the lime, taste for salt, and serve over rice with lime wedges.
de: A mild meatless curry with potatoes, chickpeas and spinach.

d:
Heat the oven to 275°F. Line a sheet pan with foil.

Flip the ribs bone-side up. Slide a butter knife under the thin membrane at one end, grab it with a paper towel and pull it off.

Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper and rub it all over the ribs.

Wrap each rack tightly in foil and bake on the pan 2½ hours, until the meat pulls back from the bones.

Unwrap, brush with BBQ sauce, and broil (or grill) 3 to 5 minutes until sticky and caramelized. Rest 5 minutes and cut between the bones.
de: Fall-off-the-bone ribs, low and slow in the oven, finished with BBQ sauce.

d:
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder and salt and rub it all over the pork.

Put the onion in the slow cooker, set the pork on top, and pour the broth and vinegar around it.

Cover and cook on low 8 to 10 hours (or high 5 to 6), until the pork shreds easily.

Lift out the pork, discard big pieces of fat, and shred with two forks. Pour off most of the liquid, return the pork, and stir in the BBQ sauce.

Pile onto toasted buns and top with coleslaw.
de: Rubbed pork shoulder cooked all day and tossed with BBQ sauce for sandwiches.

d:
Toss the chicken with the oil, brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and salt.

Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates.

Grill the thighs 5 to 6 minutes per side, until they reach 175°F.

Brush with BBQ sauce during the last 2 minutes on each side, letting it caramelize without burning.

Rest 5 minutes and serve with extra sauce.
de: Juicy boneless thighs with a sweet dry rub and a sticky BBQ finish.

d:
Set the grill for indirect heat at about 375°F (burners on one side only).

Pat the chicken dry. Rub with oil and the mixed brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper, inside and out.

Pour out (or drink) half the can of ginger ale (lemon-lime soda or beer works the same way) and set the chicken upright over it, legs forward, so it stands like a tripod.

Set it on the cool side of the grill, close the lid, and cook 1¼ to 1½ hours, until the thigh reaches 175°F.

Carefully lift the chicken off the can (use tongs and a towel; the can is very hot). Rest 10 minutes before carving.
de: A whole chicken roasted upright on the grill for crisp skin and juicy meat.

n: Grilled Kielbasa and Pineapple BBQ Skewers
d:
Soak wooden skewers 20 minutes and start the rice.

Thread the kielbasa, pineapple, peppers and onion onto the skewers.

Stir the BBQ sauce with the honey.

Grill over medium-high heat 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until the sausage is browned and the vegetables are charred. Brush with the glaze for the last 2 minutes.

Serve over rice.
de: Smoky sausage, pineapple and peppers grilled with BBQ glaze.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F.

Cook the bacon in an oven-safe pot until crisp. Add the onion and cook 4 minutes.

Stir in the beans, BBQ sauce, brown sugar, mustard and Worcestershire.

Bake uncovered 45 minutes, stirring once, until thick and bubbly.
de: Sweet and smoky baked beans with bacon, perfect with anything off the grill.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F. Pat the turkey dry. Mix the butter, garlic, thyme, sage, salt and pepper.

Loosen the skin with your fingers and rub half the butter under it and the rest over the top.

Set the turkey on the onion in a roasting pan and pour 1 cup broth into the pan.

Roast 1½ to 2 hours, until the thickest part reaches 160°F (it rises to 165°F while resting). Tent with foil if it browns too fast. Rest 20 minutes.

For gravy, pour the pan drippings into a saucepan and spoon off most of the fat. Whisk the flour into the remaining 1 cup cold broth until smooth, then whisk it into the drippings. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes, whisking, until thick. Taste for salt and pepper. Slice the turkey and serve with gravy.
de: A holiday turkey without the whole bird: herb butter, crisp skin and pan gravy.

i: 1 fully cooked spiral-cut ham (7 to 9 lb)
d:
Heat the oven to 325°F. Set the ham cut-side down in a roasting pan, add the water, and cover tightly with foil.

Bake about 12 minutes per pound, until it reaches 120°F inside.

Simmer the brown sugar, honey, Dijon, butter and cinnamon 2 minutes, until smooth.

Uncover the ham, turn the oven to 400°F, and brush on half the glaze, letting it run between the slices. Bake 10 minutes, brush with the rest, and bake 5 to 10 minutes more until glossy (140°F).

Rest 15 minutes, then cut along the bone to release the slices.
de: The holiday ham, glazed with brown sugar, honey and Dijon.

i: 1 bone-in prime rib roast (3 bones, about 6 lb)
Optional: 1/2 cup horseradish sauce, for serving
d:
The night before, rub the roast all over with the salt and refrigerate it uncovered (this seasons it deeply and dries the surface).

Take it out 2 hours before cooking. Heat the oven to 250°F. Mix the butter, garlic, rosemary, thyme and pepper and rub it over the fat side.

Roast bone-side down until the center reaches 120°F for medium-rare, about 3 to 3½ hours. Rest 30 minutes, loosely covered.

Heat the oven to 500°F and return the roast for 6 to 8 minutes, until deeply browned.

Cut the bones off, then slice across the grain. Serve with the pan juices and horseradish for the adults.
de: A special-occasion roast with a garlic herb crust, cooked low and seared hot. Salt it the night before.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the chicken very dry inside and out.

Toss the potatoes and onion with 2 tbsp oil and ½ tsp salt and spread in a roasting pan or large oven-safe skillet.
