Mix the butter with the thyme, rosemary and the rest of the salt, rub it under and over the skin, and stuff the lemon halves and garlic inside. Set the chicken on the potatoes, breast up, and drizzle with the remaining oil.

Roast 70 to 80 minutes, until the thigh reaches 175°F and the juices run clear.

Rest 15 minutes, carve, and squeeze the roasted lemon over the meat and potatoes.
de: Crisp-skinned roast chicken with lemon, garlic and potatoes in the same pan.

n: Beef Tenderloin with Garlic Herb Butter
i: 1 center-cut beef tenderloin (2 1/2 to 3 lb), trimmed and tied
d:
Take the beef out 1 hour before cooking. Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat dry and season all over with salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over high heat and sear the roast 2 minutes per side, until browned all over.

Roast 20 to 30 minutes, until the center reaches 125°F for medium-rare.

Meanwhile, mix the butter, garlic, parsley and thyme.

Spread half the butter over the hot roast and rest 15 minutes. Slice ½ inch thick and top each slice with a little more butter.
de: An easy, impressive holiday roast: seared, roasted and sliced.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Melt the butter and cook the onion, apple and celery 5 minutes. Stir in the stuffing mix, broth and sage and let cool 5 minutes.

Butterfly the pork: cut lengthwise along one side, stopping 1 inch from the other side, open it like a book, and pound to an even 1 inch. Season with 1 tsp salt.

Spread the stuffing over the pork, leaving a 1-inch border. Roll it up tightly and tie with kitchen twine every 2 inches. Rub with oil and the rest of the salt.

Roast on a rack in a pan 60 to 70 minutes. Stir the brown sugar and Dijon and brush on for the last 10 minutes, until the meat reaches 145°F.

Rest 10 minutes, remove the twine, and slice.
de: Pork loin rolled around an apple and herb stuffing, roasted until juicy.

d:
Heat the air fryer to 400°F.

Set out three dishes: flour; beaten eggs; panko mixed with parmesan, garlic powder, paprika and salt.

Dredge each tender in flour, dip in egg, and press into the crumbs.

Spray the basket and the tenders with oil. Cook in a single layer, in batches, 10 to 12 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and 165°F inside.

Serve with honey mustard (or ranch).
de: Crunchy panko tenders in the air fryer, no frying oil.

d:
Heat the air fryer to 400°F.

Pat the chops dry, rub with oil, and coat with the mixed brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and thyme.

Cook in a single layer 10 to 12 minutes, flipping halfway, until they reach 145°F.

Rest 5 minutes before serving.
de: Juicy seasoned boneless chops in about 12 minutes.

i: 1 1/2 lb chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
d:
Toss the chicken with the buttermilk and let it sit 10 minutes.

Heat the air fryer to 400°F. Mix the crushed cornflakes, parmesan, garlic powder, paprika and salt in a bag or bowl.

Lift the chicken out of the buttermilk, add to the crumbs, and shake or toss to coat well.

Spray the basket, add the nuggets in a single layer, and spray the tops. Cook 8 to 10 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and 165°F.

Serve with ketchup, honey mustard or BBQ sauce.

Plain milk works in place of buttermilk, and panko in place of cornflakes.
de: Bite-size crispy nuggets the kids can help bread.

i: 1 1/2 lb Yukon gold potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
d:
Heat the air fryer to 400°F.

Soak the cubes in cold water 10 minutes if you have time (crisper), then dry very well.

Toss with the oil, garlic powder, paprika and salt.

Cook 18 to 20 minutes, shaking the basket every 5 minutes, until golden and tender. Toss with parmesan.
de: Golden, crunchy potato cubes in the air fryer.

d:
Cut the string cheese in half. Freeze 30 minutes so they hold their shape.

Set out three dishes: flour; beaten eggs; both breadcrumbs mixed with parmesan.

Coat each piece in flour, egg and crumbs, then dip in egg and crumbs again for a sturdy crust. Freeze 15 minutes more.

Heat the air fryer to 390°F. Spray the basket and the sticks and cook in a single layer 6 to 7 minutes, until golden. Watch closely; they melt fast.

Serve right away with ranch.
de: String-cheese mozzarella sticks with a garlic butter or ranch dip.

n: Air Fryer Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs
d:
Start the rice. Heat the air fryer to 400°F.

Toss the chicken with the oil, garlic powder, paprika and salt.

Cook in a single layer 12 to 14 minutes, flipping halfway, until 175°F.

Meanwhile simmer the honey, soy sauce, garlic and butter 2 minutes.

Toss the chicken in the glaze and serve over rice.
de: Crisp-edged thighs tossed in a sticky honey garlic glaze.

i: 1 can (20 oz) pineapple chunks, with juice
d:
Put the chicken in the slow cooker with the onion and bell pepper.

Stir the pineapple and juice with the BBQ sauce, brown sugar and soy sauce and pour it over.

Cover and cook on low 4 hours (or high 2), until the chicken reaches 165°F.

Shred or slice the chicken and stir it back into the sauce. Serve over rice.
de: Chicken simmered with pineapple and BBQ sauce, served over rice.

i: 2 cans (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
1 bag (24 oz) frozen homestyle egg noodles
d:
Put the chicken in the slow cooker. Add the soup, broth, butter, thyme and pepper.

Cover and cook on low 6 hours (or high 3), until the chicken is tender.

Lift out the chicken and shred it.

Stir the frozen noodles into the cooker, cover, and cook on high 30 to 45 minutes, until tender. Stir in the chicken.

Season with salt and serve as is, or over mashed potatoes the classic Midwest way.
de: Homestyle chicken and thick egg noodles in a creamy broth, served over mashed potatoes.

n: Slow Cooker Beef Tips and Gravy
i: 3 lb beef chuck roast, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
d:
Toss the beef with the flour, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper. Brown it in the oil in batches in a hot skillet (optional but adds flavor).

Put the onion and mushrooms in the slow cooker and add the beef.

Whisk the broth, gravy mix, Worcestershire and garlic and pour it over.

Cover and cook on low 8 hours (or high 5), until the beef is fork-tender.

Cook the egg noodles and serve the beef and gravy over them (mashed potatoes work too).
de: Tender beef in rich brown gravy over egg noodles or mashed potatoes.

i: 3 leeks, white and light green parts, sliced and rinsed
2 lb Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and diced
Optional: 6 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled
d:
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the leeks with a pinch of salt and cook 8 minutes, until very soft but not browned. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

Add the potatoes, broth, bay leaf and thyme. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are falling apart.

Remove the bay leaf. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth (or leave some chunks).

Stir in the cream and season with salt and pepper.

Serve topped with chives and cheddar, with crusty bread.

Use vegetable broth to keep it meatless. Crumbled bacon on top adds protein and smoky crunch.
de: Creamy, mild and meatless; blend it smooth or leave it chunky.

d:
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the broth and thyme and bring to a boil. Stir in the rice and simmer 15 minutes, until tender.

Add the chicken and heat through 3 minutes.

Turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice and parsley. Season with salt and pepper.
de: Bright, cozy chicken soup with rice, carrots and a squeeze of lemon.

d:
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the broth and Italian seasoning and bring to a boil.

Add the tortellini and cook 5 minutes, until they float and are tender.

Lower the heat, stir in the cream, spinach and parmesan, and simmer 2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Season with salt and pepper.
de: A meatless creamy vegetable soup with cheese tortellini; no tomatoes.

n: Black Bean and Cheese Enchiladas Verde
i: 2 cans (10 oz) mild green enchilada sauce
sour cream and avocado for topping
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and spread ½ cup green sauce in a 9x13 dish.

Mash about a third of the beans in a bowl, then stir in the rest of the beans, the corn, cumin, cream cheese and 1½ cups Monterey Jack.

Fill each tortilla with about ⅓ cup of the mixture, roll up, and place seam-side down in the dish.

Pour the rest of the green sauce over the top and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.

Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbly. Serve with sour cream and avocado.
de: Meatless enchiladas with beans, corn and cheese under mild green sauce.

d:
Use cold, day-old rice and break up any clumps.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set and move to a plate.

Add the remaining oil, onion, broccoli and peas and carrots and cook 4 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the rice, spread it out, and let it toast 1 minute before stirring. Fry 3 to 4 minutes.

Add the soy sauce and eggs and toss. Finish with sesame oil and green onions.
de: Meatless fried rice loaded with eggs and vegetables.

d:
Cook the noodles per the package and drain.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer (in batches if needed) and cook 8 minutes, until deeply browned. Add the onion and cook 4 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.

Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute. Slowly stir in the broth and Worcestershire and simmer 3 minutes until thick.

Turn off the heat and stir in the sour cream. Season with salt and pepper.

Serve over the noodles with parsley.
de: A meatless stroganoff with browned mushrooms and sour cream sauce over egg noodles.

d:
Spread pesto on one side of each slice of bread.

Build sandwiches with provolone, mozzarella and tomato (salt the tomato lightly). Leave the tomato off the kids' sandwiches if they prefer.

Butter the outsides.

Cook in a skillet over medium-low heat 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden and melted.
de: Mozzarella, tomato and pesto pressed between buttery sourdough.

i: sour cream and salsa verde for dipping
d:
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pepper and onion 5 minutes. Add the beans, corn, cumin and a pinch of salt and cook 2 minutes. Move to a bowl.

Fill half of each tortilla with cheese, the vegetable mixture and more cheese. Fold over.

Wipe the skillet and cook the quesadillas over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and melted.

Cut into wedges and serve with sour cream and salsa verde.
de: Peppers, onions, black beans and corn in crispy cheese quesadillas.

i: 2 cans (15 oz) black beans, drained and patted dry
d:
Spread the beans on a sheet pan and bake at 350°F for 10 minutes to dry them out (the secret to burgers that don't fall apart). Cool 5 minutes.

Mash the beans in a bowl, leaving some chunks. Mix in the panko, egg, cheddar, cumin, garlic powder, paprika and ½ tsp salt.

Shape into 4 patties about ¾ inch thick. Chill 10 minutes if they feel soft.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side, until crisp and hot through.

Serve on toasted buns with lettuce, avocado and sauce.
de: Crisp-edged homemade black bean burgers that hold together.

d:
Cook the penne in salted water per the package. Save ½ cup pasta water and drain.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the zucchini, bell pepper, broccoli and snap peas 5 minutes, until crisp-tender. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Lower the heat and add the half and half. Simmer 2 minutes, then stir in the parmesan until smooth.

Add the pasta and toss, thinning with pasta water. Season with salt and pepper and add the tomatoes if using.
de: Spring vegetables in a light garlic parmesan cream; meatless.

d:
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Toast the orzo 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until golden.

Add the onion and cook 3 minutes, then stir in the rice for 1 minute.

Add the broth, thyme and ½ tsp salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low 18 minutes.

Let stand covered 5 minutes, then fluff and stir in the parsley.
de: Buttery toasted rice and orzo simmered in broth.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F.

Toss the green beans with the oil, garlic powder and salt on a sheet pan and spread out.

Roast 15 minutes, until blistered in spots.

Sprinkle with parmesan and roast 3 minutes more.
de: Crisp-tender roasted green beans with garlic and parmesan.

n: Corn on the Cob with Herb Butter
d:
Bring a large pot of water to a boil (don't salt it; it toughens corn). Add the corn and boil 5 to 7 minutes. Or grill over medium-high heat 10 minutes, turning, until charred in spots.

Mix the butter with the herbs, garlic powder and salt.

Brush the hot corn with herb butter and serve.
de: Sweet corn boiled or grilled and brushed with herb butter.

d:
Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, celery seed and salt.

Toss with the coleslaw mix.

Chill at least 15 minutes. Stir before serving.
de: Sweet, tangy coleslaw for BBQ night and pulled pork sandwiches.

d:
Combine the cucumber, tomatoes and onion in a bowl.

Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano and salt.

Toss and serve, or chill up to 2 hours.
de: Fresh, crunchy salad with a simple lemon dressing.

i: 2 lb sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.

Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, cinnamon and salt and spread out in a single layer.

Roast 25 to 30 minutes, flipping halfway, until tender and browned.

Drizzle with honey and toss before serving.
de: Caramelized sweet potato cubes with a touch of cinnamon and honey.

d:
Steam the broccoli 4 to 5 minutes, until bright green and tender.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk. Simmer 2 minutes until thick.

Off the heat, stir in the cheddar and garlic powder until smooth. Season with salt.

Pour over the broccoli and serve.
de: Steamed broccoli under a quick, smooth cheddar sauce kids love.

d:
Blend the cilantro, green chiles, onion, garlic and 1 cup of the broth until smooth.

Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat and toast the rice 3 minutes, stirring, until lightly golden.

Add the green mixture, the remaining broth and ½ tsp salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low 18 minutes.

Rest covered 5 minutes, then fluff.
de: Mild Mexican-style rice blended with cilantro and green chiles instead of tomato.

i: 2 cans (15 oz) pinto beans, with liquid
d:
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 4 minutes, then the garlic and cumin for 30 seconds.

Add the beans with their liquid and simmer 5 minutes.

Mash with a potato masher to the texture you like, adding a splash of water if thick.

Season with salt and top with cheese.
de: Creamy homemade refried beans from canned pintos in 15 minutes.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.

Cut the dough into 16 pieces and roll each into a 6-inch rope. Tie each in a loose knot and set on the pan.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until golden.

Stir the butter with the garlic and parsley. Brush over the hot knots and sprinkle with parmesan.
de: Soft, buttery garlic knots from store-bought pizza dough.

i: 4 cans (14.5 oz) cut green beans, drained
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F. For fresh beans, use 2 lb, trimmed and cut, boiled 5 minutes and drained.

Stir the soup, milk, soy sauce and pepper in a 2-quart baking dish. Add the beans and ⅔ cup fried onions and stir.

Bake 25 minutes, until bubbly.

Stir, top with the remaining fried onions, and bake 5 minutes more.
de: The holiday classic with crispy fried onions.

d:
Peel and cube the sweet potatoes and boil 15 minutes until very tender. Drain. Heat the oven to 350°F.

Mash with the brown sugar, butter, eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon and ½ tsp salt until smooth. Spread in a greased 9x13.

For the streusel, mix the brown sugar, flour and butter until crumbly and stir in the pecans. Sprinkle over the top (or use marshmallows).

Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the topping is golden. (If using marshmallows, add them for the last 10 minutes.)
de: Creamy sweet potatoes with a pecan streusel or marshmallow top.

d:
Spread the bread cubes on sheet pans and bake at 300°F for 15 minutes until dry. Raise the oven to 350°F.

Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the onion and celery 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the sage, thyme, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp pepper.

In a large bowl, toss the bread with the vegetables. Whisk the broth and eggs and pour over, tossing until evenly moistened.

Spread in a greased 9x13, cover with foil, and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 minutes more until golden and crisp on top.
de: Homestyle bread stuffing with celery, onion and sage.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the macaroni 2 minutes less than the package says and drain.

Melt 4 tbsp butter in a large pot, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk. Simmer 5 minutes until thick.

Off the heat, stir in 3 cups cheddar, the Monterey Jack, dry mustard, garlic powder and 1 tsp salt. Fold in the macaroni.

Spread in a greased 9x13 and top with the remaining cheddar. Melt the last 1 tbsp butter, toss with the panko, and sprinkle over.

Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbly and golden. Rest 5 minutes.
de: The holiday-style baked mac with a crunchy buttered crumb top.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and line an 8x8 pan with parchment.

Melt the butter in a microwave-safe bowl. Stir in the sugar, then the eggs and vanilla.

Stir in the cocoa, flour, salt and baking powder just until combined, then the chocolate chips.

Spread in the pan and bake 23 to 26 minutes, until a toothpick comes out with moist crumbs.

Cool completely before cutting (they finish setting as they cool).
de: Rich, chewy one-bowl brownies.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and line sheet pans with parchment.

Beat the butter and both sugars until fluffy, about 2 minutes. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.

Mix in the flour, baking soda and salt just until combined, then the chocolate chips.

Scoop 2-tablespoon balls 2 inches apart.

Bake 9 to 11 minutes, until golden at the edges but soft in the middle. Cool 5 minutes on the pan.
de: Classic chewy chocolate chip cookies.

n: Sheet Pan Chocolate Chip Cookie Bars
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and line a 9x13 (thick bars) or 10x15 pan with parchment.

Stir the melted butter with both sugars, then the eggs and vanilla.

Stir in the flour, baking soda and salt, then the chocolate chips.

Press into the pan and bake 22 to 26 minutes (9x13) or 18 to 20 minutes (10x15), until golden at the edges.

Cool before cutting into bars.
de: All the cookie, none of the scooping.

i: 1 can (8 oz) crushed pineapple, with juice
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F.

Spread the pie filling and pineapple in a 9x13 dish.

Sprinkle the dry cake mix evenly over the fruit (don't stir).

Drizzle the melted butter over the top, covering as much of the dry mix as you can.

Bake 45 to 50 minutes, until golden and bubbly. Serve warm with ice cream.
de: Three ingredients, no mixing bowl: fruit, cake mix and butter.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F. Toss the apples with the sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice and spread in a 9x9 or 8x8 dish.

Mix the oats, flour, brown sugar and cinnamon. Cut in the cold butter with your fingers until crumbly.

Scatter the topping over the apples.

Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.
de: Warm cinnamon apples under a buttery oat crumble.

d:
Whisk the pudding mix and milk 2 minutes. Whisk in the condensed milk and chill 5 minutes.

Fold in half the whipped topping.

Layer wafers, bananas and pudding in a 9x13 dish or bowl, repeating twice.

Top with the rest of the whipped topping and chill at least 4 hours so the wafers soften.
de: No-bake layers of vanilla pudding, bananas and wafers.

d:
Butter a 9x13 pan.

Melt the butter in a large pot over low heat. Add all but 1 cup of the marshmallows and stir until melted and smooth. Stir in the vanilla and salt.

Stir in the cereal, then the reserved marshmallows.

Press gently into the pan with buttered hands (pressing hard makes them dense). Cool 30 minutes and cut.
de: Extra-gooey marshmallow treats.

d:
Line a 9x13 pan with a layer of ice cream sandwiches, cutting to fit.

Spread with half the whipped topping and drizzle with half the fudge and caramel.

Add a second layer of sandwiches, the rest of the whipped topping and sauces, and the crushed cookies.

Cover and freeze at least 4 hours. Let sit 5 minutes before slicing.
de: A freezer cake from store-bought ice cream sandwiches.

i: 2 cans (8 oz) refrigerated crescent dough sheets
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 pan. Press one dough sheet into the bottom.

Beat the cream cheese, 1 cup sugar and vanilla until smooth and spread over the dough.

Lay the second dough sheet on top. Pour the melted butter over it and sprinkle with the cinnamon sugar.

Bake 30 minutes, until golden. Cool, then chill 1 hour before cutting. Drizzle with honey.
de: Crescent dough, sweet cream cheese filling and a cinnamon-sugar crust.

i: tortilla chips, celery and crackers for dipping
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F.

Stir the cream cheese, ranch and buffalo sauce until smooth. Fold in the chicken and 1 cup cheddar.

Spread in a small baking dish and top with the rest of the cheddar.

Bake 20 minutes, until bubbly. Serve with chips, celery and crackers.
de: Game-day dip, made mild with ranch; add hot sauce to the adults' bowl.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.

Unroll the dough and cut each triangle into 3 thin strips.

Wrap a strip around each sausage and set seam-side down on the pan.

Brush with egg and sprinkle with seasoning. Bake 12 to 15 minutes until golden. Serve with honey mustard and ketchup.
de: Little smokies wrapped in crescent dough with honey mustard.

d:
Bake the tots on a sheet pan per the package, until extra crispy (usually 25 minutes at 425°F).

Push them together, top with the chicken, then the cheddar and bacon.

Bake 3 to 5 minutes more, until melted.

Drizzle with sour cream stirred with ranch and sprinkle with green onions. Serve from the pan.
de: Game-day dinner: crispy tots, cheese, bacon and ranch.
nu:
Calories: 640
Protein: 34g
Carbohydrate: 42g
Fat: 37g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

i: 1 can (10 oz) mild green enchilada sauce
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13 dish.

Mix the chicken, enchilada sauce, green chiles, corn, cumin and 1 cup cheese and spread in the dish.

Stir the muffin mix with the eggs and milk until just combined and spread over the filling.

Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the cornbread is golden and a toothpick comes out clean.

Sprinkle with the remaining cheese, bake 2 minutes to melt, and rest 5 minutes.
de: Creamy green chile chicken under a sweet cornbread crust.

d:
Whisk the orange juice, lime juice, oil, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt and cilantro. Marinate the steak 30 minutes (or up to 8 hours in the fridge).

Heat the grill or a cast-iron pan to high.

Cook the steak 4 to 5 minutes per side for medium (135°F). Rest 10 minutes.

Slice thinly against the grain and chop.

Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, guacamole and lime.

Flank steak and corn tortillas are both good swaps.
de: Citrus-marinated grilled steak, sliced thin for tacos.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.

Brown the beef and drain. Stir in the taco seasoning, ⅔ cup water and the refried beans and simmer 3 minutes until thick.

Warm the tortillas so they roll without cracking. Spread 2 tablespoons filling along one edge of each, add cheese, and roll tightly.

Place seam-side down, spray with oil, and bake 15 to 18 minutes until crisp.

Serve with warm queso (or sour cream).
de: Crispy oven-baked taquitos for dipping in queso or sour cream.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 dish. Scatter the biscuit pieces in the dish.

Brown the sausage in a skillet. Sprinkle with the flour and stir 1 minute, then slowly stir in 2 cups milk and simmer until thick. Season with pepper.

Whisk the eggs with the remaining milk and ½ tsp salt and pour over the biscuits. Sprinkle with half the cheddar.

Spoon the sausage gravy over the top and sprinkle with the rest of the cheese.

Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the eggs are set and the biscuits are golden.
de: Biscuits baked into sausage gravy and eggs; breakfast for dinner.

d:
The night before, spread the bread in a greased 9x13. Whisk the eggs, milk, half and half, brown sugar, vanilla and cinnamon and pour it over. Press the bread down, cover, and refrigerate overnight.

Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix the topping ingredients with your fingers until crumbly and sprinkle over.

Bake 45 to 50 minutes, until puffed and set in the center.

Rest 5 minutes and serve with maple syrup and berries.
de: Assemble the night before, bake for a breakfast-for-dinner night.

d:
Toss the chicken with the oil, lemon zest and half the juice, the garlic, oregano and salt. Marinate 15 minutes (or up to overnight).

Cook the rice and stir in the rest of the lemon juice.

Thread the chicken on skewers and grill over medium-high heat 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until 165°F. Or cook in a hot skillet 6 to 7 minutes.

Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with a pinch of salt.

Build bowls with lemon rice, chicken, cucumber salad, feta and tzatziki.
de: Lemon-oregano chicken with rice, cucumber salad and tzatziki.

i: 2 lb Yukon gold potatoes, cut into wedges
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F.

Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano and salt. Toss half with the potatoes in a large roasting pan and pour in the broth.

Toss the chicken with the rest of the mixture and nestle it skin-side up among the potatoes.

Roast 45 to 50 minutes, until the skin is crisp, the chicken reaches 175°F and the potatoes are tender and golden.

Spoon the pan juices over everything before serving.
de: Sheet-pan chicken thighs and lemony potatoes that soak up the pan juices.

d:
Mix the beef, panko, egg, garlic powder and salt gently and roll into 1 1/2-inch meatballs.

Brown the meatballs in a large skillet over medium-high heat, 6 to 8 minutes, turning, then move to a plate. Start the noodles.

Melt the butter in the skillet and cook the mushrooms 5 minutes until browned. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth and Worcestershire.

Return the meatballs, cover, and simmer 10 minutes until cooked through (160°F).

Off the heat, stir in the sour cream. Serve over the noodles.
de: Tender beef meatballs in a creamy mushroom gravy over egg noodles.

d:
Brown the beef and onion in a deep skillet with a lid, 7 minutes. Drain the fat and season with garlic powder, paprika and 1 tsp salt.

Stir in the rice for 1 minute, add the broth, and bring to a boil.

Cover and simmer on low 15 minutes.

Scatter the corn and peas on top, cover, and cook 5 minutes more until the rice is tender.

Stir, top with cheddar, cover until melted, and serve.
de: One-pan seasoned beef and rice finished with melty cheddar.
nu:
Calories: 560
Protein: 36g
Carbohydrate: 50g
Fat: 23g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings

i: 2 lb Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cubed
d:
Boil the potatoes in salted water 15 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with the butter and milk; season with salt. Heat the oven to 400°F.

Brown the beef and onion 8 minutes and drain. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then the broth, Worcestershire and thyme. Simmer 3 minutes until thick.

Stir in the peas and carrots and spread in a 9x13 dish.

Spread the potatoes over the top, rough up with a fork, and sprinkle with cheddar.

Bake 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.
de: Savory beef and vegetables under a golden mashed potato crust.

d:
Heat the oven to 350°F. Slice the slab of rolls in half and set the bottoms in a 9x13 dish.

Layer the roast beef and Swiss, then add the tops.

Brush with the butter mixed with garlic powder. Cover with foil and bake 15 minutes, then uncover 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, simmer the broth, Worcestershire and onion powder 5 minutes for the au jus.

Cut into sliders and serve with cups of jus.
de: Roast beef and Swiss on Hawaiian rolls with warm au jus for dipping.

d:
Cook the rice and stir in the juice of the lime and the cilantro.

Brown the beef, drain, and simmer with the taco seasoning and 2/3 cup water 5 minutes.

Warm the beans and corn together.

Build bowls with rice, beef, beans and corn, cheese, sour cream and avocado. Salsa goes on the adults' bowls.
de: Taco-seasoned beef over cilantro-lime rice with all the toppings.

n: Grilled Steak and Potato Foil Packets
i: 1 1/2 lb sirloin steak, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 1/2 lb baby potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
d:
Heat the grill to high (or the oven to 450°F). Microwave the potatoes in a covered bowl 7 to 8 minutes, until nearly tender.

Toss the steak, potatoes and green beans with the butter, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper.

Divide among 4 large sheets of heavy foil in a single layer and fold into sealed packets.

Grill 10 to 12 minutes (or bake 15), flipping once, until the steak is 135°F for medium and the beans are crisp-tender.

Open carefully (hot steam) and serve from the packets. A squeeze of lemon or a drizzle of steak sauce brightens the butter.
de: Sirloin bites, potatoes and green beans in garlic butter foil packets.

d:
Start the rice per the package. Season the flour with garlic powder, paprika, 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Dredge the chops, saving 2 tbsp of the flour.

Sear the chops in the oil over medium-high heat 3 minutes per side. Move to a plate.

Melt the butter and cook the onion 6 minutes. Stir in the saved flour, then whisk in the broth and half and half.

Return the chops, cover, and simmer 10 minutes until they reach 145°F.

Serve over the rice (or mashed potatoes) with the gravy.
de: Seared pork chops simmered in a creamy onion gravy.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Rub the pork with oil, salt and paprika.

Sear in an oven-safe skillet 2 minutes per side until browned.

Stir the brown sugar, garlic, Dijon and soy sauce and spread it over the pork.

Roast 15 to 20 minutes until 145°F. Rest 5 minutes and slice, spooning the pan glaze over.
de: A sweet, garlicky glaze on juicy roasted pork tenderloin.

i: 1 lb boneless pork chops, diced small
d:
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the pork with salt and cook 5 minutes until browned. Move to a plate.

Scramble the eggs until just set and add to the pork.

Add the remaining oil, onion and peas and carrots. Cook 3 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the rice and fry 3 to 4 minutes, letting it crisp.

Stir in the soy sauce, pork and eggs. Finish with sesame oil and green onions.
de: Takeout-style fried rice with tender pork and egg.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F and start the rice.

Season the pork with salt and sear in the oil in an oven-safe skillet 2 minutes per side.

Stir the teriyaki with the honey and brush half over the pork. Roast 15 to 20 minutes until 145°F, brushing once more.

Steam the broccoli. Rest the pork 5 minutes and slice.

Serve over rice with broccoli, spooning the pan glaze over, with sesame seeds and green onions.
de: Glazed teriyaki pork tenderloin sliced over rice with broccoli.

n: Sausage, Peppers and Potatoes Sheet Pan
d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and salt and roast 15 minutes.

Add the sausages, peppers and onion tossed with the remaining oil, Italian seasoning and garlic powder.

Roast 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until the sausages reach 160°F and everything is browned.

Slice the sausages and serve.
de: Italian sausage, sweet peppers and crispy potatoes on one pan.

d:
Brown the turkey in a deep skillet, 7 minutes.

Stir in the taco seasoning, rice, beans, corn and broth and bring to a boil.

Cover and simmer on low 18 minutes until the rice is tender.

Top with cheese, cover 2 minutes to melt, and serve with sour cream and avocado.
de: Lean turkey, beans and rice in one pan, topped with cheese.

d:
Brown the turkey with the onion and pepper, 8 minutes.

Stir in the BBQ sauce, brown sugar, mustard and Worcestershire.

Simmer 10 minutes until thick.

Pile onto toasted buns.
de: Sweet and tangy sloppy joes with a BBQ base instead of tomato sauce.

d:
Season the chops with garlic powder, salt and pepper.

Sear in the oil over medium-high heat 4 to 5 minutes per side until 145°F. Move to a plate.

Add the broth, honey and Dijon to the skillet and simmer 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until syrupy.

Stir in the butter, return the chops, and spoon the sauce over.
de: Pan-seared chops in a sweet honey mustard pan sauce.

i: 2 cans (10 oz) mild green enchilada sauce
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F and spread 1/2 cup green sauce in a 9x13 dish.

Brown the beef, drain, and simmer with the taco seasoning and 1/2 cup water 5 minutes. Stir in the refried beans.

Fill each tortilla with the beef mixture and a little cheese, roll, and place seam-side down.

Pour the rest of the sauce over and top with the remaining cheese.

Bake 20 minutes until bubbly.
de: Ground beef enchiladas in mild green sauce, no red sauce at all.

i: 4 green bell peppers, halved and seeded
d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Set the pepper halves in a baking dish and bake 10 minutes to soften.

Cook the onion and mushrooms in the oil 6 minutes. Add the steak and garlic powder and cook 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Lay half a slice of provolone in each pepper, fill with the steak mixture, and top with another half slice.

Bake 15 minutes until the cheese is melted and the peppers are tender.
de: Bell pepper halves filled with shaved steak, onions and provolone.

d:
Start the rice.

Brown the pork in a large skillet 7 minutes, breaking it up. Drain most of the fat.

Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the soy sauce, brown sugar and sesame oil. Simmer 2 minutes until glossy.

Spoon into lettuce cups with carrots and green onions. Serve the rice alongside.
de: Sweet soy ground pork in lettuce cups with rice on the side.

d:
Brown the beef and drain.

Stir in the taco seasoning and 2/3 cup water and simmer 5 minutes.

Warm the shells per the package.

Set out the toppings and build tacos at the table.

Soft flour tortillas work too.
de: Taco night the way the kids like it: seasoned beef and all the toppings.

i: 1 1/2 lb Yukon gold potatoes, cut in chunks
d:
Season the roast with salt and pepper and brown it in the oil in a hot skillet, 3 minutes per side.

Put the potatoes, carrots and onion in the slow cooker and set the roast on top.

Whisk the broth, onion soup mix and Worcestershire and pour over.

Cover and cook on low 8 hours until fork-tender.

Move the roast and vegetables to a platter. Stir the cornstarch with 2 tbsp water into the liquid and cook on high 10 minutes for gravy.
de: Slow-cooked chuck roast with carrots, potatoes and rich gravy.

d:
Brown the sausage in a large skillet, 7 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the broth and cream and bring to a simmer.

Add the tortellini and simmer 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until tender.

Stir in the parmesan and spinach until wilted.
de: Cheese tortellini with sausage and spinach in a garlic parmesan cream.

d:
Cook the noodles and drain.

Whisk the soy sauce, hoisin, brown sugar and sesame oil.

Stir-fry the vegetables in the oil over high heat 4 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the noodles and sauce and toss 2 minutes.
de: Meatless lo mein loaded with vegetables.

d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Boil the tortellini 2 minutes less than the package and drain.

Stir together the tortellini, Alfredo, milk, spinach and 1 cup mozzarella in a 9x13 dish.

Top with the remaining mozzarella and parmesan.

Bake 20 minutes until bubbly and golden.
de: Meatless baked tortellini in Alfredo with spinach and mozzarella.

d:
Cook the rice and stir in the lime juice and cilantro.

Warm the beans with their liquid, cumin and garlic powder, mashing a few.

Warm the corn.

Build bowls with rice, beans, corn, cheese, avocado and sour cream.
de: Meatless burrito bowls with seasoned black beans and cilantro-lime rice.

d:
Cook the mushrooms in the oil 5 minutes. Add the spinach and garlic until wilted. Season with salt.

Fill half of each tortilla with cheese, the vegetables and more cheese. Fold.

Cook in a skillet over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.

Cut into wedges and serve with sour cream.
de: Crispy meatless quesadillas with sautéed spinach and mushrooms.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F. Rub the potatoes with oil and salt, prick them, and bake 50 to 60 minutes until tender.

Steam the broccoli 4 minutes.

Melt the butter, whisk in the flour 1 minute, then the milk. Simmer until thick and stir in the cheddar off the heat.

Split the potatoes, fluff, and top with broccoli, cheese sauce and sour cream.
de: Meatless loaded potatoes with broccoli and a cheddar sauce.

d:
Heat the oven to 425°F.

Brush the naan with the oil mixed with garlic.

Top with mozzarella, tomatoes and parmesan.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes and finish with basil.
de: Meatless flatbreads with garlic oil, fresh mozzarella and basil.

i: 1 lb Yukon gold potatoes, diced small
d:
Heat the oven to 400°F. Microwave the potatoes 5 minutes.

Melt the butter and cook the onion 5 minutes. Stir in the flour, then whisk in the broth and milk. Simmer until thick.

Add the potatoes, vegetables and thyme. Season with salt and pepper and pour into a deep pie dish.

Lay the crust over the top, crimp, and cut slits.

Bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes.
de: A meatless pot pie with creamy vegetables under a flaky crust.

d:
Heat the oven to 400°F.

Warm the refried and black beans with the cumin.

Spread the beans on the tostadas and top with cheese.

Bake 6 to 8 minutes until melted, then top with lettuce, sour cream and avocado.
de: Crunchy meatless tostadas with refried beans, cheese and toppings.

n: Baked Mac and Cheese with Broccoli
d:
Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the macaroni, adding the broccoli for the last 2 minutes. Drain.

Melt 3 tbsp butter, whisk in the flour 1 minute, then the milk. Simmer 4 minutes until thick.

Off the heat, stir in 2 1/2 cups cheddar and season with salt. Fold in the pasta and broccoli.

Spread in a 9x13, top with the remaining cheese and panko tossed with the last 1 tbsp melted butter.

Bake 20 minutes until golden.
de: A meatless dinner-sized mac and cheese with broccoli baked in.

n: Pesto Gnocchi with Peas and Parmesan
d:
Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the gnocchi straight from the package in a single layer.

Cook 5 to 6 minutes without stirring much, until golden on one side, then toss and cook 3 minutes more.

Add the peas and 2 tbsp water and cook 2 minutes until hot.

Off the heat, stir in the pesto, cream and parmesan until the gnocchi are coated.
de: Meatless pan-crisped gnocchi tossed with pesto, peas and parmesan.

n: Hot Honey Sausage and Ricotta Pizza
i: Optional: 2 tbsp hot honey, for the adults
d:
Crust: Heat the oven to 475°F with a rimmed 13x18-inch sheet pan on the lowest rack, and let the dough sit on the counter while it heats (about 20 minutes) so it stretches easily. On a sheet of parchment, press and stretch the dough into a 12x17-inch rectangle, brush with the olive oil, then slide it (parchment and all) onto the hot pan. Par-bake 6 minutes, until puffed and set but still pale. This keeps the middle from going soggy under the toppings.

While the oven heats, brown the sausage in a skillet over medium-high heat 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink remains (160°F). Drain on paper towels and wipe out the skillet.

Make the sauce in the same skillet: melt the butter over medium heat, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then whisk in the flour for 1 minute. Whisk in the milk and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until it is as thick as gravy. Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and a pinch of salt. Stir the ricotta with the lemon zest, oregano and a pinch of salt and pepper.

Spread the white sauce over the par-baked crust to within ½ inch of the edge. Scatter on the mozzarella, sausage and red onion, then drop small spoonfuls of the lemon ricotta over the top.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes more, until the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots and the bottom is golden when you lift a corner. Rest 3 minutes, then cut into 12 squares. Drizzle with honey (hot honey on the adults' squares) and tear basil over the top. The sweet-salty-creamy contrast is the whole point, so don't skip the drizzle.
de: Garlic white sauce, crumbled Italian sausage, lemony ricotta and a honey drizzle (hot honey for the adults). Sauce: 5-Minute Garlic White Pizza Sauce.
nu:
Calories: 860
Protein: 40g
Carbohydrate: 88g
Fat: 37g
Serving Size: 1 of 6 servings (2 squares)

n: BBQ Pulled Pork Pizza with Quick-Pickled Onions
i: 1 package (16 oz) refrigerated BBQ pulled pork
Optional: 1/4 cup pickled jalapeño slices, for the adults
d:
Crust: Heat the oven to 475°F with a rimmed 13x18-inch sheet pan on the lowest rack, and let the dough sit on the counter while it heats (about 20 minutes) so it stretches easily. On a sheet of parchment, press and stretch the dough into a 12x17-inch rectangle, brush with the olive oil, then slide it (parchment and all) onto the hot pan. Par-bake 6 minutes, until puffed and set but still pale. This keeps the middle from going soggy under the toppings.

Quick-pickle the onions first: microwave the vinegar, sugar and salt 1 minute, stir until dissolved, and pour over the sliced onion in a jar or bowl. Let sit at least 15 minutes (they keep 2 weeks in the fridge).

Stir the BBQ sauce, honey, smoked paprika and 1 tbsp of the pickling vinegar together. Break up the pulled pork with a fork; if it is very saucy, let it drain in a strainer so the crust stays crisp.

Spread the BBQ sauce over the par-baked crust. Top with the mozzarella, pork and cheddar.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes more, until the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots and the bottom is golden when you lift a corner. Rest 3 minutes, then cut into 12 squares. Scatter a handful of drained pickled onions and the cilantro over the top. Pickled jalapeños go on the adults' squares. Leftover pork from Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Pork works great here (about 3 cups).
de: Smoky BBQ base, pulled pork, cheddar and mozzarella, finished with tangy pink pickled onions and cilantro. Sauce: Smoky BBQ Pizza Sauce.

d:
Crust: Heat the oven to 475°F with a rimmed 13x18-inch sheet pan on the lowest rack, and let the dough sit on the counter while it heats (about 20 minutes) so it stretches easily. On a sheet of parchment, press and stretch the dough into a 12x17-inch rectangle, brush with the olive oil, then slide it (parchment and all) onto the hot pan. Par-bake 6 minutes, until puffed and set but still pale. This keeps the middle from going soggy under the toppings.

While the oven heats, cook the chopped bacon in a large skillet over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes, until crisp. Drain on paper towels. Stir the cream cheese, ½ cup parmesan, milk, garlic and pepper until smooth.

Spread the parmesan base over the par-baked crust and top with the mozzarella and bacon. Bake 4 minutes.

Pull the pan out, use a spoon to make 6 shallow nests in the cheese, and crack an egg into each. Bake 6 to 8 minutes more, until the whites are fully set and the yolks are still soft (go 2 to 3 minutes longer for firm yolks).

Sprinkle with the remaining parmesan, parsley and a generous grind of black pepper. Rest 3 minutes and cut so each square gets an egg. A few drops of hot sauce or chili crisp is the grown-up finisher.
de: A garlicky parmesan cream base, crisp bacon, mozzarella and six eggs baked right on top, finished with lots of black pepper.

d:
Crust: Heat the oven to 475°F with a rimmed 13x18-inch sheet pan on the lowest rack, and let the dough sit on the counter while it heats (about 20 minutes). Stir the oil, garlic and oregano together. On a sheet of parchment, stretch the dough into a 12x17-inch rectangle, brush with 1 tbsp of the garlic oil, slide it onto the hot pan and par-bake 6 minutes, until puffed and set but still pale.

Toss the chicken with half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.

Brush the rest of the garlic oil over the par-baked crust. Top with the mozzarella, chicken, feta, olives (keep them to one half if the kids aren't olive fans) and red onion.

Bake 8 to 10 minutes more, until the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots and the bottom is golden when you lift a corner. Rest 3 minutes, then cut into 12 squares.

Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Scatter over the hot pizza and drizzle with tzatziki. The cold, crunchy, tangy topping against the hot cheese is what makes this one.
de: Garlic-herb olive oil base, lemon-oregano chicken, feta, olives and red onion, topped after baking with cool cucumber and tzatziki. Sauce: Garlic-Herb Pizza Oil.
nu:

i: Optional: 1/2 tsp chili powder, for the adults
d:
Crust: Heat the oven to 475°F with a rimmed 13x18-inch sheet pan on the lowest rack, and let the dough sit on the counter while it heats (about 20 minutes) so it stretches easily. On a sheet of parchment, press and stretch the dough into a 12x17-inch rectangle, brush with the olive oil, then slide it (parchment and all) onto the hot pan. Par-bake 6 minutes, until puffed and set but still pale. This keeps the middle from going soggy under the toppings.

Char the corn: melt the butter in a large skillet over high heat, add the corn in an even layer and leave it alone 3 minutes, then stir and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until browned in spots. Season with salt. Toss the chicken with the cumin and smoked paprika.

Stir the cream cheese, mayonnaise, lime zest, half the lime juice and the garlic powder until smooth. Spread over the par-baked crust. Top with the Monterey Jack, chicken and corn.

Heat the oven to 325°F and line a 9x9 pan with parchment, leaving some hanging over the sides.

Stir the graham crumbs, melted butter and 2 tbsp sugar, press firmly into the pan and bake 8 minutes.

Beat the cream cheese until smooth, then beat in the yogurt, ⅔ cup sugar, cornstarch, vanilla, lemon zest and 2 tbsp lemon juice. Beat in the eggs one at a time on low just until blended (overbeating causes cracks).

Pour over the crust and bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly. Turn off the oven, crack the door and let it cool inside 30 minutes.

Chill at least 3 hours, then lift out and cut into 16 bars with a hot knife. Top with berries.
de: Creamy, tangy cheesecake bars made lighter with Greek yogurt and reduced-fat cream cheese on a graham crust.

i: Optional: 1 cup sliced strawberries, for serving
d:
Melt the chocolate chips in the microwave in 20-second bursts, stirring between, until smooth.

Put the cottage cheese, melted chocolate, cocoa, maple syrup, vanilla and salt in a blender or food processor.

Blend 1 to 2 minutes, scraping down once, until completely smooth with no curds left. Taste and add a little more maple syrup if you like it sweeter.

Spoon into 5 small cups and chill at least 30 minutes to firm up. Top with strawberries or a little whipped cream.
de: Blended cottage cheese, cocoa and melted chocolate chips make a silky chocolate mousse with 11 g protein per cup. Nobody will guess.

d:
Toss the strawberries with the sugar and lemon juice and let them sit 10 minutes until juicy.

Beat the cream cheese until smooth, then beat in the Greek yogurt, honey and vanilla until fluffy.

Layer the yogurt, strawberries and their juice, and graham crumbs in 6 glasses or jars, ending with crumbs on top.

Serve right away for crunchy crumbs, or chill up to 1 day for a softer, cheesecake-like texture.
de: Whipped Greek yogurt and cream cheese layered with sweet strawberries and graham crumbs. Tastes like cheesecake, about 11 g protein each.

d:
Stir the peanut butter, honey, vanilla and salt in a bowl until smooth (microwave 15 seconds if stiff).

Stir in the oats, flaxseed, chocolate chips and protein powder if using. If the mix is too dry to hold together, add milk 1 tbsp at a time.

Chill 20 minutes so it is easier to roll, then roll into 20 balls about 1 inch across.

Keep in the fridge up to 1 week or freeze up to 3 months.
de: No-bake bites of oats, peanut butter, honey and mini chocolate chips. A dessert or after-practice snack.

d:
Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.

Stir the yogurt, honey and vanilla until smooth. Spread on the parchment about ½ inch thick (roughly 9x13 inches).

Scatter the strawberries, blueberries, chocolate chips and granola over the top and press them in lightly.

Freeze at least 3 hours, until firm. Break into pieces and serve right away; it softens fast. Store in a freezer bag up to 1 month.
de: Honey-sweetened Greek yogurt spread on a sheet pan with berries and chocolate, frozen and broken into pieces.

n: Banana Chocolate Chip Greek Yogurt Snack Cake
d:
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x9 pan or line it with parchment.

In a large bowl, whisk the mashed bananas, yogurt, eggs, brown sugar, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

Sprinkle the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt over the top and stir just until no dry flour remains. Fold in most of the chocolate chips.

Spread in the pan, scatter the remaining chips on top and bake 28 to 32 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.

Cool at least 15 minutes before cutting into 12 squares.
de: A moist, one-bowl banana snack cake made with Greek yogurt and less sugar, studded with chocolate chips.

n: Chocolate Peanut Butter Banana Nice Cream
d:
Slice ripe bananas and freeze them on a plate or in a bag at least 4 hours ahead (keep a bag in the freezer for this).

Put the frozen banana, peanut butter, cocoa, yogurt and milk in a food processor or strong blender.

Blend 2 to 3 minutes, scraping down often, until it looks like soft-serve. Add another splash of milk if it won't move.

Taste and blend in honey if you want it sweeter. Serve right away, or freeze 1 hour for a scoopable texture.
de: Frozen bananas blended with peanut butter, cocoa and Greek yogurt into soft-serve. No ice cream maker needed.
